summary: Research a zero-cost stack, Quran data licensing, Persian/English NLU, RAG abstention, and architecture for a free public Quran Q&A chatbot
logs: [research:rag-abstention] failed: API Error: provider closed the stream before sending a completion marker (upstream connection ended mid-stream)
Verification: 30 claims corrected or downgraded; 43 flagged as cost/legal-critical

research.topic: Free LLM inference APIs for a public, $0, English + Persian Quran Q&A chatbot (verified late October 2026)

findings.claim: Google Gemini API still has a free tier in October 2026, but Google no longer publishes fixed per-model RPM/RPD quotas; they are account-specific and visible only in AI Studio.
findings.detail: Free plan: limited access to certain models, free input/output tokens, and 'Content used to improve our products'. The pricing page marks several Flash-class models 'Free of charge'; Gemini 2.5 Flash and 2.5 Flash-Lite are still listed in the 2026-10-28 docs. The rate-limits page (last updated 2026-10-28) says limits depend on usage tier and must be viewed at aistudio.google.com/rate-limit; RPD resets at midnight Pacific. Last published 2025 values for gemini-2.5-flash were 10 RPM / 250 RPD / 250,000 TPM, and for gemini-2.5-flash-lite 15 RPM / 1,000 RPD / 250,000 TPM; these must be confirmed in AI Studio. The Free plan is positioned 'for developers and small projects getting started', with production pushed to paid tiers; no explicit public-app ban was found. Streaming is supported.

findings.claim: OpenRouter ':free' models are capped at 20 requests/minute and 50 requests/day, or 1,000/day after at least $10 in lifetime credit purchases (higher tier granted from 9 credits).
findings.detail: The limits table is: less than 10 credits purchased all-time = 20 RPM / 50 RPD; at least 10 = 20 RPM / 1,000 RPD. The higher daily ceiling is granted starting one credit below the threshold (currently 9 credits) to absorb top-up fees. Caps are per account/API key and are shared by every end user of a public app; the doc gives no public-app exemption. Free variants are model IDs ending in ':free'; paid variants have no platform-level request cap. The daily counter is exposed as free_model_daily_requests. A one-time $10 purchase is enough even if the balance is later spent down. Streaming is supported (mid-stream rate-limit errors arrive as SSE events).

findings.claim: Cloudflare Workers AI includes 10,000 Neurons per day free, reset at 00:00 UTC; using more requires the Workers Paid plan.
findings.detail: Free-tier math at ~1,000 input + 400 output tokens per short answer: @cf/zai-org/glm-4.7-flash (131,072-token context; 5,500 neurons/M input, 36,400/M output) is about 20 neurons/request, roughly 500 answers/day; @cf/openai/gpt-oss-120b (128,000 ctx; 31,818 + 68,182) is about 59, roughly 169/day; @cf/deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 (262,144 ctx; 27,273 + 109,091) is about 71, roughly 141/day; @cf/qwen/qwen3.8-27b (262,144 ctx; 40,909 + 290,909) is about 157, roughly 64/day. @cf/meta/llama-3.3-70b-instruct-fp8-fast has only a 24,000-token context and the Llama 3.3 Community License, and is weaker for Persian. All listed models support SSE streaming via stream:true. Cloudflare states: 'Cloudflare does not use Customer Content processed by Workers AI to train AI models.'

findings.claim: GroqCloud's current rate-limit documentation publishes only Developer-plan base limits and no free plan.
findings.detail: Developer-plan base limits shown: openai/gpt-oss-120b = 30 RPM / 1,000 RPD / 8K TPM / 200K TPD; qwen/qwen3.8-27b = 30 RPM / 1,000 RPD / 8K TPM / 200K TPD; openai/gpt-oss-safeguard-20b = 3 RPM / 1,000 RPD / 2K TPM / 200K TPD. The page says 'Upgrade to Developer plan' and 'the limits shown below are the base limits for the Developer plan'. No free-tier table, free price, or free-plan statement appears; groq.com/pricing redirects to the homepage. Treat Groq as paid-only unless the signed-in console shows a Free plan.

findings.claim: Cerebras has no ongoing free tier in October 2026; its entry offer is a one-time $5 promotional credit that requires a valid payment method and expires 30 days after activation.
findings.detail: The Developer tier is 'For development, evaluation, and experimentation; not intended for production use.' Models and prices: GPT OSS 120B at $0.35/M input and $0.75/M output; Qwen 3.8 27B at $0.99/M input and $1.49/M output, about 1,850-3,000 tokens/s. The credit is non-transferable and has no cash value; API and Playground access pause when it expires or is exhausted unless PayGo credits are separately purchased. No free RPM/RPD table is published.

findings.claim: Mistral's API Free mode still exists, but Mistral explicitly describes it as 'intended for evaluation and prototyping' and does not publish its exact RPS/TPM/monthly-token limits.
findings.detail: Free mode is the default and has the lowest limits. Three limits are enforced: requests per second, tokens per minute (input + output), and tokens per month; a 429 means one was exceeded. The exact numbers are shown only on the Admin panel Limits page (admin.mistral.ai/plateforme/limits). Pay-as-you-go unlocks Tier 1; Tier 2 is over $20 billed, Tier 3 over $100, Tier 4 over $500. Current API ids include mistral-small-2603 ($0.15/$0.60 per M) and ministral-8b-2512 ($0.15/$0.15 per M). Persian is not a first-class Mistral language, so expect weaker Farsi than Gemini/Qwen.

findings.claim: NVIDIA build.nvidia.com NIM endpoints are free to prototype at up to 40 RPM for most models, with no per-token billing but a prototyping-only positioning.
findings.detail: FAQ wording: 'All models on build.nvidia.com are free to prototype with'; 'The free tier runs on rate limits - up to 40 requests per minute (RPM) for most models, with no per-token billing. Your personal rate limit is shown in the top-right of the dashboard.' Production use requires deploying a NIM container or using a partner endpoint. Model ids visible include deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash, nvidia/nemotron-3.5-super-vl-120b-a12b, nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning-30b-a3b, and nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b. No daily request cap is published.

findings.claim: Z.ai's only $0 chat models are GLM-4.7-Flash and GLM-4.5-Flash; GLM-5.3-Flash is paid at $0.15/M input and $0.50/M output.
findings.detail: The Z.AI pricing table lists GLM-4.7-Flash and GLM-4.5-Flash as Free for input, cached input, cached storage, and output. GLM-5.3-Flash: $0.15 input, $0.03 cached input, $0.50 output; 1M-token context and 128K max output. GLM-4.7-Flash is 128K-class (Cloudflare's mirror lists 131,072 tokens). Rate limits and concurrency are shown at z.ai/manage-apikey/rate-limits, not in public docs. Streaming is documented. Z.AI is China-based; review data residency/terms before sending user questions.

findings.claim: SambaNova's no-payment Free Tier allows 20 RPM, 20 requests/day, and 200,000 tokens/day.
findings.detail: Free Tier is applied when no payment method is linked; Developer Tier (with a payment method) gets 60 RPM / 12,000 RPD and is capped at 20M tokens/day across all models. Free-tier production models: DeepSeek-V3.1, Meta-Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct, and gpt-oss-120b; preview models DeepSeek-V3.2 and gemma-4-31B-it are also free. The 20 RPD cap makes this unusable for public traffic except as a demo or emergency fallback.

findings.claim: Cohere trial keys allow 1,000 API calls/month and 20 requests/minute per chat model.
findings.detail: Trial keys are described as 'evaluation keys (free but limited in usage)'. Chat models with 20 req/min each: Command A+, Command A Reasoning, Command A Translate, Command A Vision, Command A, Command R+, Command R, Command R7B, and North Mini Code. Other trial limits: Embed 2,000 inputs/min, Rerank 10 req/min, Tokenize 100 req/min, Parse and default endpoints 500 req/min; audio transcription 5 req/min. The rate-limit page does not explicitly ban production or commercial use, but 1,000 calls/month is about 33/day.

findings.claim: Alibaba Cloud Model Studio gives new users 1,000,000 free tokens per model (input + output combined), valid for 90 days, in the Singapore region only.
findings.detail: Each model has an independent quota; snapshot and latest versions are separate models with separate quotas. Free quota covers real-time inference only. 'Free Quota Only' mode stops requests with error AllocationQuota.FreeTierOnly when the quota is exhausted, preventing charges. Requires completing account information; re-registering does not grant another quota. Eligible Qwen models include qwen3.8-max and qwen-plus in the Singapore region. After 90 days or exhaustion, billing switches to pay-as-you-go.

findings.claim: GitHub Models was fully retired on July 30, 2026; its playground, model catalog, inference API, and BYOK are no longer available.
findings.detail: GitHub's docs state: 'As of July 30, 2026, GitHub Models has been fully retired. The playground, model catalog, inference API, and bring your own key (BYOK) are no longer available to any customer.' GitHub redirects users to Azure AI Foundry for model access or GitHub Copilot for GitHub-integrated AI. Do not design the Quran chatbot around GitHub Models.

findings.claim: Hugging Face free accounts receive zero Inference Providers credits; only PRO ($2/month) or Team/Enterprise organizations get $2/month in credits.
findings.detail: The pricing table shows Free Users monthly credits: None; free users must purchase credits or upgrade to PRO. PRO gets $2.00/month; Team/Enterprise gets $2.00 per seat per month. Credits are general compute credits (usable across Inference Providers, Inference Endpoints, Spaces/ZeroGPU, Jobs) and are applied before pay-as-you-go. Routed requests are billed at provider rates with no Hugging Face markup.

findings.claim: Chutes explicitly offers no free tier, and Together AI and DeepSeek publish only paid per-token pricing with no free quota.
findings.detail: Chutes FAQ: 'We do not offer a free tier at this time. Top up your account in the app to get started.' Together's serverless pricing lists paid rates such as GLM-5.3-Flash $0.15/$0.50 per M and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash $0.30/$1.20; the 'Start for free' wording is marketing, with no free allowance shown. DeepSeek is paid per token: deepseek-flash (V4.1-Flash-1017, 1M context) at $0.15/$0.60 per M off-peak and $0.30/$1.20 peak; deepseek-v4-pro at $0.66/$1.98 off-peak and $1.32/$3.96 peak. No free quota is listed.

findings.claim: Novita lists Apodex 1.1 Mini as a $0 model with 256K context; no other free chat models or published rate limits were found.
findings.detail: The Novita pricing table shows 'Apodex 1.1 Mini 256K Free Free'. Other models are paid, e.g. Ling 3.0 Flash at $0.06/M input and $0.18/M output, and Ling 3.1 Flash 1019 at $0.30/$0.90. No rate-limit documentation was found (the rate-limit doc URLs return 404), and the model is obscure with unverified Persian quality. Treat it only as an extra fallback, not a primary provider.

findings.claim: No live 2026 Persian benchmark covering Gemini free tier, Qwen, GLM, or DeepSeek was found; the only current Farsi evaluation repo tests OpenAI, Anthropic, and OpenRouter models only.
findings.detail: heyparsadev/persian-llm-eval v1.1 (leaderboard generated 2026-10-08) has 544 scored items across 21 tracks and 23+ runs. Top results: GPT-5.5 0.970 public_eval, Claude Opus 5.5 0.957 practical. It contains no Gemini, Qwen, GLM, or DeepSeek free-tier results. Therefore the Persian ranking in this report is qualitative: Gemini is likely strongest, Qwen3.8/GLM-4.7/DeepSeek are credible, and Llama-3.3-70B and Mistral Small are weaker. Validate on 50-100 native-written Farsi questions before launch.

research.caveats: Several official pages were blocked or login-gated, so exact quotas could not be verified for every provider: OpenRouter's terms page and Groq's console returned 403/Cloudflare blocks; Z.ai's rate-limit page redirects to a login; Gemini's per-model quota table now exists only inside AI Studio; Mistral publishes Free-mode limits only in its admin console. The Gemini 2.5 Flash 10 RPM / 250 RPD / 250K TPM figures are the last publicly published values (2025) and may be stale in 2026. Fireworks, Hyperbolic, Moonshot, and SambaNova's full terms could not be verified in this pass; Fireworks and Hyperbolic are usually signup-credit-only rather than ongoing free tiers, but that is not confirmed here. ToS caveats matter for a public app: Gemini free-tier content is used to improve Google products; NVIDIA is prototyping-only; Mistral Free is evaluation/prototyping; Cohere trial keys are evaluation keys; Cerebras is a 30-day promo requiring a card. No free tier found here is sized for 'many users' — realistic combined capacity is roughly 1,000-2,000 short answers/day with strict rate limiting, caching, and provider fallback. Prices, limits, and model line-ups change frequently; every fact is date-stamped 2026-10-31 unless the source states otherwise.
research.recommendation: Primary pick: Google Gemini API free tier (gemini-2.5-flash, or the current Flash model AI Studio shows as free) — qualitatively the strongest Persian output among these free options, English is native, and it gives roughly 250 requests/day at $0, but free-tier content is used to improve Google products, so add a clear privacy notice. Runner-up: Cloudflare Workers AI with @cf/zai-org/glm-4.7-flash as the default (about 500 short answers/day from 10,000 Neurons, no training on customer content, production-friendly) and @cf/qwen/qwen3.8-27b for harder Persian questions (about 64/day). For extra headroom, route a third slice to Z.ai glm-4.7-flash (free) and OpenRouter ':free' after a one-time $10 purchase (1,000 requests/day). Expect a realistic combined ceiling near 1,000-2,000 answers/day, not mass scale.

research.topic: Free embedding and reranking stack for a bilingual English/Persian Quran Q&A chatbot (6,236 verses, Arabic source + EN/FA translations)

findings.claim: Cloudflare Workers AI gives 10,000 Neurons/day free and charges $0.011 per 1,000 Neurons; bge-m3 and Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B both cost 1,075 Neurons per million input tokens, equivalent to $0.0118/M input tokens and about 9.3M free embedding tokens/day.
findings.detail: Current rate card (last updated 2026-10-20): bge-small-en-v1.5 1,841 Neurons/M, bge-base-en-v1.5 6,058/M, bge-large-en-v1.5 18,582/M, bge-m3 1,075/M, plamo-embedding-1b 1,689/M, qwen3-embedding-0.6b 1,075/M. At ~40 tokens/verse, 1,000 vectors = 40k tokens = 43 Neurons = $0.00047 paid. A full Arabic+English+Persian index (~6,236 x 3 x 40 = 748k tokens) costs ~804 Neurons, about 8% of one day's free allocation. Derived free capacity: ~232k 40-token vectors/day or ~310k 30-token query embeddings/day, before the Workers Free 100k requests/day cap and D1 row-read limits.

findings.claim: Cloudflare's hosted bge-m3 is a 1024-d, 100+ language model, but its docs claim a 60,000-token context, contradicting BAAI's 8,192-token model configuration; Cloudflare's Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B is 1024-d with MRL 32-1024 but is capped at 8,192 tokens versus 32K upstream.
findings.detail: BAAI bge-m3 config: xlm-roberta, hidden_size 1024, max_position_embeddings 8194, MIT license, dense+sparse+multi-vector. Cloudflare page says 60,000 tokens; the architecture uses absolute XLM-R position embeddings, so 60k is almost certainly a docs error. Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B: hidden_size 1024, max_position_embeddings 32768, Apache 2.0, MRL 32-1024; Cloudflare page caps context at 8,192. Both Cloudflare endpoints cost $0.0118/M input tokens.

findings.claim: Cloudflare Vectorize Free stores only 5M vector dimensions and serves 30M queried dimensions/month, so 6,236 verses x 1024-d = 6.39M stored dimensions does not fit bge-m3, and a top-20 query at 512-d consumes 10,240 dimensions, allowing only ~2,900 queries/month.
findings.detail: Storage math: 6,236 x 1024 = 6,385,664 dims (over 5M by 28%); 768-d = 4,789,248 (fits); 512-d = 3,192,832 (fits); 384-d = 2,394,624. Query budget at 512-d: topK 10 = 5,859 queries/month, topK 20 = 2,929/month, topK 50 = 1,172/month; at 1024-d topK 20 = 1,465/month. D1 Free is the $0 alternative: 5GB storage, 5M rows read/day, 100k rows written/day, 2MB max row/500MB max DB, and D1 supports FTS5. Storing 6,236 int8 vectors in D1 costs 3.19MB at 512-d or 6.39MB at 1024-d; seven 1,000-vector BLOB chunks (512KB-1MB each) means 7 rows read/query, ~714k queries/day within the 5M row-read budget. D1 BLOB scanning removes the Vectorize query cap but shifts cost to Worker CPU: 6.4M int8 MACs/query at 1024-d, 3.2M at 512-d; use a WASM SIMD cosine kernel or FTS-prefilter to <=500 candidates to stay near the 10ms free CPU limit.

findings.claim: Cloudflare Workers AI's only reranker is @cf/baai/bge-reranker-base at $0.00311/M tokens, but BAAI lists that model as Chinese+English only, so it is not suitable for a Persian/Arabic Quran retrieval stack.
findings.detail: bge-reranker-base is a 278M-parameter XLM-R-base cross-encoder with a 512-token maximum; Cloudflare pricing is $0.00311/M input tokens (~283 Neurons/M), so 10k free Neurons cover ~35M rerank tokens/day (top-20 x ~100 tokens = 2,000 tokens/query, ~17.7k queries/day). A search of the Cloudflare Workers AI catalog on 2026-10-31 found no other reranker (no bge-reranker-v2-m3, no Qwen3-Reranker); the only match is bge-reranker-base. Using it on Arabic/Persian is an out-of-distribution use with no published benchmark.

findings.claim: Gemini's embedding endpoints are free of charge on the free tier: gemini-embedding-2 (3072-d default, 8,192 input, multimodal) and gemini-embedding-001 (3072-d default, 2,048 input), with paid text prices of $0.20/M and $0.15/M respectively; free-tier rate limits are no longer published on the docs page, but a 2025-12-19 Google forum answer lists 100 RPM / 30k TPM / 1,000 RPD for gemini-embedding-001.
findings.detail: Both models output 3072-d by default and support MRL truncation across 128-3072 (recommended 768/1536/3072); gemini-embedding-2 auto-normalizes truncated dims, gemini-embedding-001 requires manual normalization below 3072. Batch price is half ($0.10/M and $0.075/M). At 40 tokens/vector, 1,000 vectors cost $0.006 (001) or $0.008 (2). The 2026-10-28 rate-limits page says limits depend on usage tier and can be viewed in Google AI Studio; the Dec-2025 forum figure is the last concrete published number found, so treat 1,000 RPD as unverified for 2026. The Gemini API docs/pricing pages returned HTTP 403 from this network and were read through the r.jina.ai text proxy.

findings.claim: Jina jina-embeddings-v3 is 1024-d, 8192-token, CC BY-NC 4.0 with MRL 32-1024, but only 30 languages were tuning targets (Arabic included, Persian not); jina-embeddings-v4 is 4B parameters/2048-d/32K under the Qwen Research License; Jina's own pricing page returned HTTP 451 from this network and third-party 2026 free-token claims conflict (1M, 10M, and 10K).
findings.detail: v3 ONNX is fp32 2291MB / fp16 1147MB with no official int8 file; it is based on Jina-XLM-RoBERTa. v4 supports dense and multi-vector, 2048-d default, MRL 128-2048, 32,768 tokens, 30+ languages. Jina's API is hosted on AWS US-East/EU-Frankfurt. APIRank (updated 2026-10-30) lists $0.02/M tokens for Embeddings v3 and 10K free; aicredits.dev claims 10M shared tokens across Embeddings/Reranker/Reader/Classifier; yangmao.ai claims 1M. The official page was legally blocked (451), so none of these free-tier numbers could be verified first-hand; do not build a $0 plan on Jina without manual verification from an allowed region.

findings.claim: Cohere trial keys allow Embed at 2,000 inputs/min and Rerank at 10 requests/min but cap at 1,000 API calls/month and are explicitly not permitted for production or commercial use; Rerank 5/4/3.5 are single multilingual models covering 100+ languages.
findings.detail: Cohere docs rate limits: trial 1,000 API calls/month; Chat 20 req/min; Embed 2,000 inputs/min; Rerank 10 req/min; Parse/default 500 req/min. The pricing page states trial calls are free but 'trial keys are rate limited and are not permitted to be used for production or commercial purposes', which disqualifies a public site. Rerank model IDs are rerank-v5.0-pro/fast, rerank-v4.0-pro/fast, and rerank-v3.5; a search unit is one query with up to 100 documents. The current pricing page only showed Model Vault instance pricing (e.g. Rerank 5 Fast Medium $4.00/hr, $2,500/month), not a per-1,000-search rate.

findings.claim: Voyage AI gives one-time free allowances of 200M tokens for voyage-4-large/voyage-4/voyage-4-lite/voyage-context-4 and 50M for voyage-multilingual-2, with list prices of $0.12/$0.06/$0.02 per M tokens; rerank-3 is $0.05/M with a 200M-token free allowance listed in the pricing table.
findings.detail: Voyage-4 family: 32,000-token context, 1024-d default with MRL 256/512/2048. Prices: voyage-4-large $0.12/M, voyage-4 $0.06/M, voyage-4-lite $0.02/M; voyage-multilingual-2 $0.12/M with 50M free. Rerank-3/3-lite have 32k context; pricing table lists rerank-3 $0.05/M (estimated $0.0025/request at 100 docs x 500 tokens) and rerank-3-lite $0.02/M, both with 200M free tokens, while the prose says the first 200M free applies to rerank-2.5/2.5-lite/2/2-lite - a page inconsistency. The free allowances are 'first N tokens ... for every account', i.e. one-time, not monthly. At 40 tokens/vector, 1,000 embeddings cost $0.0008 (lite), $0.0024 (voyage-4), or $0.0048 (large).

findings.claim: Mistral's current API price list has mistral-embed at $0.10/M tokens (8k context) and codestral-embed at $0.15/M, with no free embedding allowance documented; Hugging Face Inference Providers gives free accounts no monthly credits, while PRO gets $2.00/month.
findings.detail: Mistral model page: mistral-embed-2312, GA, 8k context, $0.10/M input, performance rating 2/5; codestral-embed-2505 is $0.15/M. The pricing markdown lists only paid embedding rates and free moderation, so there is no evidence of a current free API embedding tier. Hugging Face pricing: Free users have 'None' monthly credits and must purchase credits or upgrade; PRO users get $2.00/month; hf-inference is mostly CPU inference for embeddings/ranking but is still credit-billed. Mistral-embed's 1024-d output size is widely documented but was not stated on the pages fetched, so treat that dimension as medium confidence.

findings.claim: BAAI bge-m3 is a 568M-parameter, 1024-d, 8192-token MIT model with the strongest measured Arabic/Persian MIRACL scores among the open models checked: ar 78.4 / fa 60.9 dense, rising to 80.2 / 63.4 with all retrieval modes, versus BM25 39.5 / 28.7 and multilingual-e5-large 76.0 / 59.0.
findings.detail: MIRACL nDCG@10 (18-language table): bge-m3 dense ar 78.4, fa 60.9; dense+sparse ar 79.6, fa 62.3 (+1.2/+1.4); all modes ar 80.2, fa 63.4. This is direct evidence that a lexical hybrid adds a small but measurable gain and that BM25 alone is far weaker, especially for Persian. ONNX sizes: fp32 2266.8MB, fp16 1134.0MB, int8 568.5MB, q4f16 699.9MB. Int8 dynamic-quantized exports exist (optimum per-channel/AVX2) and the Transformers.js q8 path works, but no official int8 retrieval-quality benchmark was found, so validate on a held-out Quran query set before committing.

findings.claim: multilingual-e5-small/base/large are 118M/278M/560M-parameter, 384/768/1024-d, 512-token, MIT models; e5-small ONNX is 118MB int8 / 235MB fp16 / 470MB fp32, making it the best browser/WASM fallback, with MIRACL 16-language nDCG@10 of 60.8/62.3/66.5 and e5-large at ar 76.0 / fa 59.0.
findings.detail: e5-small: 117,654,272 params, 384-d, max_position 512; e5-base: 278,044,162 params, 768-d, 514; e5-large: 559,890,946 params, 1024-d, 514. All list Arabic and Persian in their language metadata and are MIT. ONNX int8 sizes: 118.1MB / 278.7MB / 561.8MB. The multilingual-E5 technical report reports MIRACL averages of 60.8 (small), 62.3 (base), 66.5 (large), 65.7 (large-instruct); the BGE-M3 paper's per-language table gives e5-large ar 76.0 / fa 59.0. paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2 is the same 118M/384-d size class, Apache 2.0, but has a 128-token max sequence and older quality - use only as a tiny baseline, not for serious retrieval.

findings.claim: EmbeddingGemma-300m is ~303M params/768-d/2048-token under the Gemma license with QAT q4/q8 (ONNX q8 309MB, q4 197MB, fp32 1234MB), but it cannot use fp16 and Transformers.js WebGPU q4/q8 produced cosine ~0 versus WASM in an open 2026-07-22 issue; use WASM q8 or WebGPU fp32. EmbeddingGemma 2 (740M total, 270M text backbone, 768-d, 8K, Apache 2.0) scores 61.36 MTEB multilingual versus 61.15 for v1.
findings.detail: v1: 100+ languages, MRL 768/512/256/128, 2K context, MTEB Multilingual v2 61.15/54.31 at 768d. ONNX community note: activations do not support fp16 or derivatives; use fp32/q8/q4. q8 308.9MB, q4 196.7MB, q4f16 175.4MB, fp32 1234.5MB. Issue #1728 (open, 2026-07-22) reports WebGPU q4/q8 embeddings essentially orthogonal to WASM/fp32 on Chrome 150/RTX 5060 Ti; fp32 WebGPU is correct. v2 is multimodal, 740M total (270M text + 170M vision + 300M audio), 768-d, 8K context, MRL 128-768, Apache 2.0, MTEB multilingual 61.36; it is the better-licensed current equivalent if you do not need v1's Gemma terms.

findings.claim: Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B is 596M params/1024-d/32K under Apache 2.0 with MRL 32-1024 and MTEB multilingual mean 64.33; its ONNX is 613.5MB int8 / 1200MB fp16 / 2400MB fp32, while Qwen3-Embedding-4B is 4.02B params/2560-d/32K.
findings.detail: 0.6B: 595,776,512 params, hidden_size 1024, max_position 32768, 28 layers, instruction-aware (+1-5% typical), MTEB Multilingual Mean(Task) 64.33, Retrieval 64.64. ONNX sizes: int8 613.5MB, q4f16 567.5MB, fp16 1199.9MB, fp32 2400.6MB. 4B: 4,021,774,336 params, hidden_size 2560, max_position 40960, 32K context per card, Apache 2.0; too large for browser/mobile but viable on a server GPU. No per-language Arabic/Persian MTEB split was found in the model card or paper, so its ar/fa quality is an aggregate inference, not a measured number.

findings.claim: For Arabic/Persian reranking, BAAI bge-reranker-v2-m3 is the strongest open option checked (MIRACL 69.32, BEIR 56.51, 568M params, 8192 context, Apache 2.0, int8 570MB); Jina reranker v3 (0.6B, 131k context, CC BY-NC) scores BEIR 61.94/MIRACL 66.83, Jina v2 (278M, 1024 context, CC BY-NC) MIRACL 63.65, and mxbai-rerank-base-v2 (494M, 32k, Apache 2.0) MIRACL 55.32; tiny client-side options are mmarco MiniLM (118M, 512 tokens, Arabic but not Persian) and English-only ms-marco MiniLM (22.7M, int8 23MB).
findings.detail: The Jina v3 model card publishes a common comparison table: bge-reranker-v2-m3 MIRACL 69.32/BEIR 56.51; jina-reranker-v3 66.83/61.94; jina-reranker-v2 63.65/57.06; mxbai-rerank-base-v2 55.32/58.40; Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B 57.70/56.28. bge-reranker-v2-m3 ONNX: fp32 2271MB, fp16 1136MB, int8 570.7MB; jina-reranker-v2 int8 279.6MB. Client-side: cross-encoder/mmarco-mMiniLMv2-L12-H384-v1 is 117.6M params, 512 tokens, Apache 2.0, trained on 14 languages including Arabic but not Persian; ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2 is 22.7M params, 512 tokens, English-only, 23MB int8. Cohere Rerank trial is not production-legal, and Cloudflare's only hosted reranker is EN/ZH-only, so a $0 Arabic/Persian reranker is not available as a hosted service.

findings.claim: SQLite FTS5 unicode61 is not usable on diacritized Arabic without pre-normalization: in SQLite 3.50.4 it tokenized the Basmala into fragments ['الر','الل','ب','ح','س','م','ن','ه','يم'], remove_diacritics 2 changed nothing, and exact 'رحمن' did not match 'الرحمن'; Persian ZWNJ split 'می‌خواهم' into 'می'+'خواهم' while 'میخواهم' stayed one token.
findings.detail: FTS5 docs confirm remove_diacritics only removes Latin-script diacritics; Arabic tashkeel (U+064B-065F, U+0670, U+06D6-06ED) and tatweel U+0640 must be stripped in the app before indexing. Normalize alef variants (آأإٱ->ا), ya (ى->ي), ta marbuta (ة->ه or keep consistently), Persian yeh/kaf (ي->ی, ك->ک), and ZWNJ/ZWJ -> space or empty. Then index a normalized surface column plus a light-stem column (strip Arabic prefixes ال/و/ف/ب/ك/ل and common suffixes) or use the trigram tokenizer for substring/root-ish matching. D1 supports FTS5 including fts5vocab but exposes only built-in tokenizers (unicode61/ascii/porter/trigram); custom C tokenizers cannot be loaded. PostgreSQL ships a Snowball Arabic stemmer (src/backend/snowball/libstemmer/stem_UTF_8_arabic.c) but no Persian stemmer file. JS options: lunr-languages 1.23 ships lunr.ar.js and lunr.fa.js; MiniSearch supports custom tokenize/processTerm with no built-in stemming; FlexSearch advertises an Arabic charset; npm has arabic-stem and persian-normalize, but no maintained persian-stemmer package.

findings.claim: Transformers.js v3 reports WebGPU up to 100x faster than WASM; estimated single-query latency on a laptop is e5-small 10-30ms WebGPU/30-80ms WASM-q8, EmbeddingGemma 40-120ms WebGPU-fp32/150-400ms WASM-q8, Qwen3-0.6B 150-400ms WebGPU-fp16/1-3s WASM-q8, and bge-m3 150-500ms WebGPU-fp16/1.5-4s WASM-int8; a Worker cannot self-host any of these because Workers cap memory at 128MB.
findings.detail: Workers limits: 128MB memory, 10ms CPU/request on Free, 5min on Paid. Model files: e5-small q8 118MB, EmbeddingGemma q8 309MB, Qwen3-0.6B q8 613MB, bge-m3 int8 568MB - all exceed or tightly press the 128MB Worker limit once ONNX Runtime and activations are added, so the only viable Worker path is the Workers AI binding (remote GPU), not in-Worker ONNX. Latency figures are analytical estimates from 2 x params x tokens FLOPs at ~100 GFLOPS CPU / 2-5 TFLOPS GPU, not measured on the target device. Batched 1,000-vector estimates: e5-small 2-5s WebGPU / 20-60s WASM; bge-m3 30-90s WebGPU / 30-90min WASM. At $0.30-0.50/hr GPU, 1,000 bge-m3 vectors (~10-30s) cost ~$0.001-0.004; on a $5/month CPU VPS, 5-10 minutes costs <$0.01; in the user's browser the marginal cost is $0. Workers AI binding total is roughly 100-500ms (50-200ms network + 50-300ms inference), but Cloudflare publishes no latency SLA.

research.caveats: Read-only research; no project files were modified. All provider facts are date-stamped 2026-09-29 to 2026-10-31 and free tiers change frequently. Key unresolved/contradictory points: (1) Cloudflare's bge-m3 page says 60,000-token context while BAAI's config says 8,192 - treat 60k as a likely docs error and test actual truncation. (2) Gemini's 2026 rate-limits page no longer publishes numeric free-tier limits; 100 RPM/30k TPM/1,000 RPD comes from a 2025-12-19 Google forum answer and may have changed - check AI Studio for the project. (3) Jina's official pricing page returned HTTP 451 from this network (legal block), and third-party 2026 free-token claims conflict (1M vs 10M vs 10K); Jina cannot be assumed usable from Iran without a proxy/manual verification. (4) Qwen3-Embedding has no published per-language Arabic/Persian MTEB split, only the 64.33 multilingual aggregate. (5) bge-m3 int8 has no official retrieval-quality benchmark; dynamic int8 may lose a few nDCG points. (6) Browser/GPU latency and self-hosted throughput are analytical estimates, not measurements on the user's hardware. (7) Cohere does not publish a per-1,000-search price on its current pricing page, and its trial is explicitly not for production. (8) Mistral-embed's 1024-d output was not stated on the fetched pages. (9) Cosine and reranker scores are not calibrated across models; a refusal threshold for 'no relevant Quranic text' must be tuned on labeled English and Persian queries, not copied from another model. (10) Vectorize free-tier query math depends on topK; the 30M queried-dimensions/month cap, not Workers AI's 10k Neurons/day, is the binding constraint for a public vector-search deployment.
research.recommendation: Primary ($0): Cloudflare Workers AI @cf/baai/bge-m3 for embeddings (1024-d, MIT upstream, proven MIRACL Arabic 78.4 / Persian 60.9, 1,075 Neurons/M tokens = ~9.3M free tokens/day; full trilingual 6,236-verse index ~0.75M tokens = ~804 Neurons, under 10% of one day's free allocation). Store vectors as int8 BLOBs in D1 (6.4MB total; seven 1,000-vector chunks of ~1MB each) and scan all 6,236 x 1024 with a small WASM SIMD cosine kernel, or FTS-prefilter to <=500 candidates; do not use Vectorize Free as the primary index because its 5M stored/30M queried dimensions per month cannot hold 6.39M bge-m3 dimensions and allows only ~1,500-2,900 top-20 queries/month. Add D1 FTS5 BM25 over normalized Arabic/English/Persian text and fuse with reciprocal rank fusion; pre-strip tashkeel, fold alef/ya/ta-marbuta, normalize Persian yeh/kaf/ZWNJ, and add a light-stem column. Reranking: do NOT use Cloudflare's only hosted reranker, @cf/baai/bge-reranker-base, for Arabic/Persian - BAAI lists it as Chinese+English only. At $0, skip the cross-encoder and use RRF plus the answer LLM's relevance/refusal check (calibrate the threshold on labeled bilingual queries). If you need a real multilingual reranker, Voyage rerank-3 (200M free tokens one-time, then $0.05/M, 32k context) is the cheapest hosted option; self-hosting BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3 (Apache 2.0, int8 570MB, MIRACL 69.32) gives the best open quality but needs a GPU for acceptable latency. Runner-up embedding: @cf/qwen/qwen3-embedding-0.6b (same $0.0118/M, 1024-d with MRL to 512, MTEB multilingual 64.33, Apache 2.0) - choose it if you want a 512-d/3.19MB index that fits Vectorize's 5M stored-dimension cap or halves D1 scan cost; its Arabic/Persian quality is not separately benchmarked. Best browser-only fallback: multilingual-e5-small q8 (384-d, 118MB ONNX, MIT) in Transformers.js WASM; EmbeddingGemma-300m q8 (309MB) is viable but only via WASM q8 or WebGPU fp32 because WebGPU q4/q8 is currently broken.

research.topic: Quran data sources and redistribution licensing for a free English+Persian Quran chatbot

findings.claim: Tanzil Quran text is CC BY 3.0 with a no-modification restriction, requiring attribution to Tanzil Project and a link to tanzil.net on any public site.
findings.detail: Text License page: "Permission is granted to copy and distribute verbatim copies of this text, but CHANGING IT IS NOT ALLOWED"; the source (Tanzil Project) must be clearly indicated and a link made to tanzil.net; the copyright notice must be reproduced in derived files. Release 1.1 (Feb 2021) ships six variants (Simple, Simple Plain, Simple Minimal, Simple Clean, Uthmani, Uthmani Minimal), each 6,236 verses. The repo file D:\Drive G - Personal\=== Personal Project\Faater.art\Faater\Resources\quran-simple.txt has 6,236 verse lines plus a 28-line copyright block at lines 6239-6266 ("Copyright (C) 2007-2026 Tanzil Project"); it differs from Tanzil's default simple download in 3,071/6,236 verses because it was generated with pause marks and tatweel (U+0640), so it is a Tanzil download-option variant, not a hand-edited text.

findings.claim: Tanzil's 115 translations (17 English, 13 Persian) are licensed for non-commercial use only, with a backlink required when more than three are used.
findings.detail: Tanzil translations page: "The translations provided at this page are for non-commercial purposes only. If used otherwise, you need to obtain necessary permission from the translator or the publisher. If you are using more than three of the following translations in a website or application, we require you to put a link back to this page... Redistributing the following list in another website is not allowed, unless direct permission is granted by the Tanzil Project." The catalog has 115 translations in 44 languages (17 English, 13 Persian). A free ad-free site fits "non-commercial"; adding ads, sponsorships or a paid tier would not. quran-json's audit reads the terms more strictly as "Tanzil translations and transliteration: non-commercial use only, no redistribution."

findings.claim: Tanzil metadata supplies surah/juz/hizb/rub/page/manzil/sajda mappings and Arabic/English/transliteration names, but no Persian surah names; sajda and juz counts conflict across free sources.
findings.detail: quran-data.xml is license="cc-by" (CC BY 3.0, copyright 2008-2009 Tanzil.info) and gives sura names in Arabic, English and transliteration, plus revelation order/place, rukus, start line, juz, hizb, rub, manzil, ruku, page and sajda. Verified counts: 114 surahs, 6,236 ayahs, 30 juz, 60 hizb, 240 rub, 604 pages, 7 manzils, 556 rukus, 15 sajdas. It has no Persian names: quran.com /chapters?language=fa returns translated_name in English, and QUL's "Surah names" resource is Arabic + Latin only. Conflicts: Tanzil and alquran.cloud list 15 sajdas including 22:77, while quran.com exposes 14 (22:77 sajdah_number=null); quran.com /juzs returns 60 objects (duplicate juz sets) for 30 juz.

findings.claim: QuranEnc exposes a keyless JSON API with 76 translations in 56 languages (3 English, 1 Persian) and permits verbatim republishing under seven conditions.
findings.detail: Endpoints: https://quranenc.com/api/v1/translations (catalog), /translation/sura/{key}/{sura}, /translation/aya/{key}/{sura}/{aya}; no API key or auth. Catalog on 2026-10-31: 76 translations in 56 languages, 3 English (english_rwwad, english_saheeh, english_hilali_khan) and 1 Persian (persian_ih, Rowwad Translation Center, v1.1.3). Terms: contents may be downloaded and re-published if (1) no modification/addition/deletion, (2) credit the publisher and QuranEnc.com, (3) state the version number, (4) keep transcript information, (5) report notes to QuranEnc, (6) update to the latest version, (7) no inappropriate advertisements. No published rate limit; responses are Cache-Control: no-store and Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *.

findings.claim: Sahih International is available for free redistribution through QuranEnc's english_saheeh edition, which matches quran.com translation id 20.
findings.detail: QuranEnc english_saheeh (Noor International Center, v1.1.2, updated 2025-06-24) matches quran.com id 20 "Saheeh International" at 1:1, 2:255, 112:1 and 18:10 apart from footnote markers. Required credit: Noor International Center and QuranEnc.com plus version 1.1.2, no wording changes, no inappropriate ads. By contrast quran-json's audit states: "Saheeh International via Tanzil: all rights reserved. The Saheeh edition QuranEnc grants is published." Use QuranEnc's copy, not Tanzil's en.sahih, for a redistributable Sahih International.

findings.claim: api.quran.com/api/v4 still works unauthenticated but is the legacy surface; QF's new Content API uses OAuth2 and publishes no rate limits.
findings.detail: Legacy host returned HTTP 200 without credentials on 2026-10-31, with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, no RateLimit-* headers, header x-qf-origin: qf-nonfaceing-data-legacy-api-quran, and Cache-Control: public, max-age=691200 (8 days). Catalog: 126 translations in 69 languages (2 Persian: IslamHouse id 135, Hussein Taji id 29), 20 tafsirs (3 English, 0 Persian). QF's migration guide says "The endpoints, query parameters, and response shapes remain the same"; the base URL moves to https://apis.quran.foundation/content/api/v4/... and auth becomes OAuth2 client credentials. Treat legacy as undocumented and subject to shutdown.

findings.claim: QF's new Content API requires OAuth2 client credentials, serves only surahs 1-2 in prelive, and keeps rate-limit values confidential.
findings.detail: Prelive base https://apis-prelive.quran.foundation, production https://apis.quran.foundation; token endpoint https://oauth2.quran.foundation/oauth2/token with grant_type=client_credentials&scope=content; every Content request needs x-auth-token and x-client-id. Without those headers the API returns HTTP 400 "The request is missing required headers or is invalid". Prelive contains only Al-Fatihah and Al-Baqarah; production access requires approval in the Developer Console. Developer Terms section 7 makes "rate-limit values" QF Confidential Information, so no public RPM/RPD numbers exist.

findings.claim: QF Developer Terms allow ads and donations but prohibit caching content over one week, redistribution, and building ML models from QF content without consent.
findings.detail: Terms last updated 2026-10-11. Allowed without a separate commercial license: charging, subscriptions, in-app purchases, display advertising, donations and freemium, provided content is part of the end-user experience and not sold, sublicensed or redistributed. Prohibited: caching or storing QF Content longer than 1 week unless obtained through Content Sync (with a next sync at least every 7 days); extracting or scraping outside API responses; using QF Content or User Data "to build advertising profiles, biometric identifiers, or machine-learning models without written consent." "Derived Materials" explicitly includes AI-generated responses and remains subject to the content restrictions. A vector index or embeddings built from QF content is therefore a legal risk; use Tanzil text for indexing.

findings.claim: quran/quran.com-data is deleted (HTTP 404), while risan/quran-json is the current static mirror but is CC BY-SA 4.0 with only one Persian edition.
findings.detail: https://github.com/quran/quran.com-data returns 404; GitHub API also 404s quran/quran.com-data and quran/quran-data; the quran org repo list has no data repository. risan/quran-json: CC BY-SA 4.0, 130 editions in 81 languages, 15 scripts, 3 transliterations, 10 English and 1 Persian edition (Rowwad). Its audit says "Tanzil translations and transliteration: non-commercial use only, no redistribution"; "Quran.com API: personal, non-commercial terms"; "QUL and Tarteel resources: no licence stated"; "fawazahmed0 quran-api: no licence per edition." CC BY-SA share-alike means a derived database may need to be released under CC BY-SA 4.0.

findings.claim: QUL is a download-only library whose per-resource licence tabs disclaim copyright information, so it cannot serve as a license basis.
findings.detail: QUL homepage: 198 translations, 220 tafsirs. Resources page: "Resources included in QUL are intended for you to download and package with your own project; no API is available." Licence tabs checked on /resources/tafsir/169 (Persian IslamHouse), /resources/tafsir/35 (Ibn Kathir), /resources/quran-metadata/70 (Surah names) and /resources/quran-metadata/64 (Sajda) each say "We don't have copyright information for this resource." QUL has 3 Persian translation resources (IslamHouse, Persian wbw, Hussein Taji) and 2 Persian tafsirs (Al-Mukhtasar, As-Saadi), but provides no rights grant.

findings.claim: spa5k/tafsir_api is MIT-licensed code with no stated data license, and its Asbab al-Nuzul edition duplicates Kashf al-Asrar.
findings.detail: Repo MIT, 210 stars, updated 2026-10-29; README advertises 123 tafsirs and "No Rate Limits". Data is generated from QUL SQLite exports and altafsir.com; no separate data license is stated. Persian editions are only persian-mokhtasar and fr-tafsir-as-saadi (misnamed slug). Bug: /tafsir/en-asbab-al-nuzul-by-al-wahidi/1.json returns the same text as /tafsir/en-kashf-al-asrar-tafsir/1.json ("In terms of allusion ... lords of recognition"), so the Asbab al-Nuzul feed is mislabeled or corrupt.

findings.claim: everyayah.com has no license terms, while alquran.cloud/Islamic Network permits non-commercial text and audio reuse and enforces about 12 requests per second per IP.
findings.detail: EveryAyah direct files: https://everyayah.com/data/Alafasy_128kbps/001001.mp3 (HTTP 200) and Persian https://everyayah.com/data/translations/Fooladvand_Hedayatfar_40Kbps/001001.mp3 (200); Makarem is at /data/translations/Makarem_Kabiri_16Kbps/. Its "Quran Text" is per-ayah GIF images, not plain text; no terms/license page was found; quran-json lists EveryAyah as "unknown". alquran.cloud terms (updated 14 June 2026): text may be reproduced, embedded, stored and displayed "for any non-commercial purpose"; commercial reproduction needs no permission from them but requires acknowledgement; translations are "contributed by their rights-holders or sourced from public-domain editions"; audio is free non-commercial. Live headers show RateLimit-Limit: 12/sec; the knowledgebase says about 10 requests/sec per IP plus a cumulative 70 requests every 7 seconds for API and CDN, HTTP 429 on breach. CDN patterns: /quran/audio/{bitrate}/{edition}/{1-6236}.mp3 and /quran/images/{surah}_{ayah}.png.

findings.claim: English translation licensing: Sahih International via QuranEnc and Talal Itani's ClearQuran are freely redistributable; Pickthall and Yusuf Ali are public domain with US date caveats; Khattab, Abdel Haleem and Shakir are not freely licensed.
findings.detail: Sahih International: QuranEnc english_saheeh, 7 conditions, credit Noor International Center + QuranEnc, v1.1.2. Talal Itani ClearQuran: CC BY-ND 4.0 plus permission to reformat/convert, credit "Translation by Talal Itani, ClearQuran.com". Pickthall (1930, d. 1936): public domain in life+70 since 2007 and in the US from 1 Jan 2026 per the Cornell chart. Yusuf Ali (1934, d. 1953): public domain in life+70 since 2024, but US public domain from 1 Jan 2030. Khattab's The Clear Quran (2016) is (c) 2025 Al-Furqaan Foundation and a registered trademark; no free redistribution grant found; quran.com's website uses resourceId 131 but the public v4 catalog (126 entries) omits it and /quran/translations/131 returns empty. Abdel Haleem (2004, OUP) is copyrighted and only displayable through quran.com API id 85. Shakir's authorship/date is disputed (Wikipedia's 1866-1939 figure is contested), so do not assume public domain; Tanzil hosts it only under non-commercial terms.

findings.claim: Persian translation licensing: Tanzil's 13 Persian editions are non-commercial only, while Saffarzadeh, Haddad Adel and Elmi are absent from every free catalog and are copyrighted or unverified.
findings.detail: Tanzil has 13 Persian translations: Ansarian, Ayati, Bahrampour, Gharaati, Elahi Ghomshei, Khorramdel, Khorramshahi, Sadeqi Tehrani, Safavi, Fooladvand, Mojtabavi, Moezzi and Makarem Shirazi, all under Tanzil's non-commercial-only terms. Saffarzadeh, Haddad Adel and Elmi are absent from Tanzil (115), QuranEnc (76), QUL (198), quran.com (126) and quran-json (130). Saffarzadeh died in 2008; Iran's 2010 amendment sets copyright at life+50, so her translation is protected to 2058. Haddad Adel (b. 1945) is living. "Elmi" could not be matched to any edition; treat it as unverified. QuranEnc's only Persian is Rowwad (persian_ih). QUL has IslamHouse, Persian wbw and Hussein Taji; quran.com has IslamHouse and Hussein Taji; quran-json has Rowwad. fawazahmed0 has 14 Persian editions including Ansarian and Makarem but no per-edition license, so it is not a license basis.

findings.claim: Free tafsir coverage is limited to a few English titles and two Persian titles; the named Persian tafsirs are absent and require permission.
findings.detail: quran.com v4 exposes 20 tafsirs (3 English: Ibn Kathir abridged, Maarif-ul-Quran, Tazkirul Quran; 0 Persian). QUL has 220 tafsirs but only 2 Persian (Al-Mukhtasar, As-Saadi). tafsir_api has 123 tafsirs, with English including Ibn Kathir, Maarif-ul-Quran, Tanwir al-Miqbas, Al-Jalalayn and Al-Mukhtasar, and only 2 Persian (Al-Mukhtasar, As-Saadi). None of Tafsir Nemouneh, Al-Mizan, Tafsir Noor, Qaraati or Kanz al-Daqa'iq appears in these catalogs; Nemouneh (Makarem, living), Noor (Qaraati, living) and Al-Mizan (Tabatabai, d. 1981) are copyrighted, while Kanz al-Daqa'iq is a classical Hanafi text whose Arabic may be public domain but whose modern edition/translation is not. Classical Arabic matns are public domain; their English/Persian translations are separately copyrighted. Asbab al-Nuzul has no reliable free feed because tafsir_api's edition is a duplicate of Kashf al-Asrar.

research.caveats: Not legal advice; verify with counsel before launch. QF production approval and rate limits are not public and its terms can change. Some statuses are inferred from publication dates or absence from catalogs, not from signed permission letters: Shakir authorship is disputed, "Elmi" is unidentified, and Tanzil's non-commercial permission may not bind individual translators. QUL provides no license data. WebSearch was unavailable in this session, so facts come from direct fetches on 2026-10-31 rather than search-engine corroboration. Iran's copyright term is from Wikipedia and US public-domain dates are from the Cornell chart updated 2026-01-01. The legacy quran.com API could be shut off without notice.
research.recommendation: Primary: keep Resources/quran-simple.txt verbatim with its copyright block and add a visible "Quran text: Tanzil Project, CC BY 3.0" link; use Tanzil quran-data.xml for surah/juz/hizb/rub/page/manzil/sajda metadata. For English use QuranEnc english_saheeh (Sahih International, credit Noor International Center + QuranEnc v1.1.2) and optionally Talal Itani ClearQuran (CC BY-ND 4.0, credit line). For Persian use QuranEnc persian_ih (Rowwad) plus Tanzil fa.ansarian, fa.makarem, fa.fooladvand, fa.bahrampour and fa.ghomshei under the non-commercial terms; add a static 114-entry Persian surah-name map. Do not build embeddings from QF, QUL, spa5k or everyayah content; do not use Saffarzadeh, Haddad Adel or Elmi. Runner-up: bundle risan/quran-json (CC BY-SA 4.0) + QuranEnc and accept share-alike, but it has only one Persian translation.

research.topic: Persian/Arabic language engineering for a bilingual (English/Persian) Quran Q&A chatbot retrieving against Arabic Quranic text (read-only research; live checks done 2026-10-31)

findings.claim: The repo's Resources/quran-simple.txt is NOT the undiacritized Tanzil 'simple' text its filename implies; it is fully vowelled Quranic text.
findings.detail: Verified locally: 6,236 verse lines with exactly 3 pipe fields (surah|ayah|text), plus 28 comment lines and 2 blank lines = 6,266 total. Character counts: U+064E fatha 121,886; U+0650 kasra 46,642; U+0652 sukun 37,372; U+064F damma 37,320; U+0651 shadda 23,016; U+064B fathatan 3,742; U+0670 superscript alef 3,330; U+0640 tatweel 939; U+06D6-U+06DC waqf marks 4,551; U+0622 alef-madda 1,511; U+0626 yeh-hamza 1,182; U+0624 waw-hamza 673. Zero ZWNJ (U+200C), zero Arabic-Indic or Persian digits, zero U+0671 alef-wasla, zero small high letters U+06E1/U+06E2.

findings.claim: Plain substring search of ordinary Quranic words returns zero hits against the repo file.
findings.detail: grep for the plain word 'الرحمن' = 0 matches in 6,236 verses. The file stores it as U+0627 U+0644 U+0631 U+0651 U+064E U+062D U+0652 U+0645 U+064E U+0640 U+0670 U+0646 U+0650 ('الرَّحْمَـٰنِ'), i.e. a tatweel U+0640 immediately followed by superscript alef U+0670 inside the word. A normalization/strip pass at index-build time is mandatory before any lexical retrieval.

findings.claim: Tanzil publishes six distinct Quran text types; only 'Simple Clean' is intended for search.
findings.detail: Uthmani ('similar to Medina Mushaf'), Uthmani Minimal, Simple ('Quran text in Imlaei script'), Simple Plain, Simple Minimal ('suitable for embedding in other texts'), Simple Clean ('without any diacritics or symbols. Suitable for easy search'). The naming is a trap: a project that downloads quran-simple.txt gets Imlaei script WITH diacritics, not a search-ready file.

findings.claim: Hazm 0.12.1 is MIT-licensed, released 2026-04-01, and its normalizer converts Arabic yeh/kaf and all digit forms in fixed translation tables.
findings.detail: PyPI JSON: hazm 0.12.1, license MIT, summary 'Persian NLP Toolkit', upload_time 2026-04-01T18:55:42. In hazm/constants.py: TRANSLATION_SRC/DST is a ~700-char 1:1 table mapping Arabic yeh U+064A to Persian yeh U+06CC, Arabic kaf U+0643 to Persian kaf U+06A9, teh marbuta U+0629 to heh U+0647, and Arabic Presentation Forms-B (U+FB50-U+FEFF) to base forms. NUMBERS_SRC='0123456789%٠١٢٣٤٥٦٧٨٩' -> NUMBERS_DST='۰۱۲۳۴۵۶۷۸۹٪۰۱۲۳۴۵۶۷۸۹' (everything becomes Persian digits, and '%' becomes '٪').

findings.claim: Hazm's diacritics removal is too narrow for Quranic text and would leave thousands of marks behind.
findings.detail: DIACRITICS_PATTERNS = [(r'[ًٌٍَُِّْ]', '')] — only U+064B-U+0652. It does NOT remove U+0670 superscript alef (3,330 occurrences in this file), U+0640 tatweel (939), or Quranic annotation signs U+06D6-U+06ED (4,551+). Also its default digit direction (ASCII -> Persian) is wrong for building a canonical search index, which should key on ASCII digits.

findings.claim: Parsivar 0.2.3.1 normalizes in the opposite digit direction and applies Persian-specific letter folding that is destructive to Arabic Quran text.
findings.detail: PyPI: parsivar 0.2.3.1, released 2024-01-02, MIT. normalizer.py maps Persian AND Arabic-Indic digits to ASCII (۰|٠ -> 0 ... ۹|٩ -> 9), maps alef variants ٲ|ٱ|إ|ﺍ|أ -> ا, ك/ڪ/ﻚ -> ک, ى|ي|ﻯ|ﻱ -> ی, and ة|ہ|ھ|ﻩ|ۀ|ە -> ه, strips tatweel U+0640 plus the six basic harakat, and converts '¬' (U+00AC) to ZWNJ U+200C. Applying this to the Arabic corpus would collapse teh marbuta into heh and alef-maqsura into yeh before indexing — acceptable only as a deliberate recall-oriented search fold, never to the displayed Quran text.

findings.claim: 'parsidate' is not a Persian text-normalization library; it is a Jalali/Persian calendar package family.
findings.detail: PyPI /pypi/parsidate/json returns 404 (no such project). GitHub repository search returns only Jalali date/time libraries: wordpress-parsi/wp-parsidate (GPL-2.0, 85 stars, WordPress Solar Hijri calendar), mahdyaralipor/parsidate (MIT, PHP Jalali date), parsicore/parsidate (Apache-2.0, Rust Jalali calendar), alisadeghiaghili/parsidate (Apache-2.0, Python Jalali date). Do not budget engineering time for it as a normalizer; use Hazm or Parsivar instead.

findings.claim: ZWNJ (U+200C) is Persian-only and must be handled asymmetrically: inserted/kept in Persian queries, stripped before matching Arabic.
findings.detail: Hazm's normalizer joins token pairs with an explicit ZWNJ character and rewrites the verb prefix with re.sub(r'^(ن?می)', r'\1‌', ...), turning 'میکنم' into 'می‌کنم'. Parsivar maps the typographic not-sign '¬' to U+200C. The Quran file contains 0 ZWNJ, so any ZWNJ surviving from a Persian query ('کتاب‌ها', 'می‌خواهد') must be deleted (or treated as a word separator) before comparing with Arabic tokens; otherwise exact-match recall is zero for those terms.

findings.claim: Alfanous (LGPL-3.0) implements the canonical Quran-search normalization chain in a reusable open-source package.
findings.detail: Alfanous-team/alfanous: 285 GitHub stars, LGPL-3.0, last push 2026-06-14. pyarabic/normalizers.py functions: stripTashkeel; stripTatweel; normalize_lamalef (lam-alef ligatures U+FEF5-U+FEFC -> lam+alef); normalize_hamza (_ALEFAT = alef-madda, alef-hamza-above, alef-hamza-below, hamza-above, hamza-below -> ALEF; _HAMZAT = waw-hamza, yeh-hamza -> HAMZA); normalize_spellerrors (TEH_MARBUTA -> HEH, ALEF_MAKSURA -> YEH); normalize_uthmani_symbols (MINI_ALEF->ALEF, ALEF_MADDA->ALEF, ALEF_WASLA->ALEF, strip [ۖ-ۭ]).

findings.claim: quran-search-engine (MIT, TypeScript) has the most complete modern normalization regex, but its final character filter deletes Persian letters and cannot be applied to Persian queries.
findings.detail: adelpro/quran-search-engine: 38 stars, MIT, pushed 2026-10-07. removeTashkeel strips [ً-ٰٟۖ-ۜ۟-۪ۨ-ۼ]. normalizeArabic then .normalize('NFC'), strips [ٰـ], maps [إأآٱ]->ا, [ؤئء]->ء, ى->ي, and finally .replace(/[^ء-ي\s-]+/g,''). That last range excludes پ U+067E, چ U+0686, ژ U+0698, گ U+06AF and Persian yeh U+06CC — so Persian input is blanked. Fork or parameterize the filter.

findings.claim: Root-based search is feasible with the Quranic Arabic Corpus v0.4 morphology file, which is small enough to ship as a static index.
findings.detail: Streamed count of quranic-corpus-morphology-0.4.txt: 6,236 distinct verses; 77,429 distinct word positions (the corpus site commonly cites 77,430); 128,219 morphology segments; 1,642 distinct ROOT: values and 4,832 distinct LEM: values. File size 6,309,503 bytes (~6.3 MB) plain text. Each line is tab-separated: (surah:ayah:word:segment), form, tag, features, and ROOT:/LEM: appear in the features column in Buckwalter transliteration (e.g. $Am, $An, $El).

findings.claim: The Quranic Arabic Corpus license is GPL plus an explicit no-modification clause, which is a serious constraint for a public website.
findings.detail: Header of quranic-corpus-morphology-0.4.txt: 'Copyright (C) 2011 Kais Dukes', 'License: GNU General Public License', 'Permission is granted to copy and distribute verbatim copies of this file, but CHANGING IT IS NOT ALLOWED', 'This annotation can be used in any website or application, provided its source (The Quranic Arabic Corpus) is clearly indicated, and a link is made to http://corpus.quran.com', copyright notice must be reproduced in derived works. Version is 0.4; site states 6,236 verses/114 chapters. This combines copyleft with a no-derivatives restriction — get legal review or use a permissively licensed alternative (e.g. MAQAM-Quranic-Corpus from CAMeL-Lab, license marked 'Other'/NOASSERTION).

findings.claim: A practical root-search architecture is: morphology map from Buckwalter root to every surface word, plus a lemma map, with query-time root expansion.
findings.detail: quran-search-engine's API takes quranData + morphologyMap + wordMap and exposes search(query, data, morphologyMap, wordMap, {lemma:true, root:true, semantic:true}). Its English-Arabic guide shows the non-Arabic path needs a hand-built concept map, e.g. {english:['truth','verity','trueness','accuracy'], arabic:['حق','صدق']} — stored as roots only, then root expansion finds 'الحق','بالحق','حقا','صدق','صدقا','بالصدق'. Without such a map, an English or Persian query cannot reach Arabic roots; this is where an LLM translation step (EN/FA -> Arabic search terms) belongs, not in answer generation.

findings.claim: Corpus morphology tags use Buckwalter ASCII transliteration, not Arabic script, so a conversion table is required before display or matching.
findings.detail: Observed ROOT:/LEM: values are strings such as $Am, $An, $Eb, $El, $Er, $HH, $Hm and lemmas such as $a>on, $aAEir, $aA^'a. Buckwalter maps '>' to hamza, '$' to shin, 'E' to ayn, etc. Build a BW->Arabic table (and its inverse) or reuse an existing pyarabic/quranic-corpus converter; otherwise root keys will never match an Arabic-script query.

findings.claim: Quran typography requires dedicated Quranic fonts and generous line-height; Vazirmatn is the standard Persian UI face, but exact font metrics were not live-verified in this session.
findings.detail: Standard choices: Amiri Quran (SIL OFL 1.1, designed for Quranic text with full harakat), KFGQPC Uthmanic Hafs (King Fahd Complex Uthmanic script, the glyph set matching Medina-Mushaf orthography), and Vazirmatn (SIL OFL 1.1) for Persian UI strings. Practical rules: set line-height >= 1.8-2.0 for fully vowelled Arabic so stacked marks (shadda+fatha, superscript alef) do not clip; use font-display: swap; subset to Arabic + Latin; avoid letter-spacing (breaks Arabic joining); set dir='rtl' and lang='fa'/'ar' per element. Treat these font license/metric claims as LOW confidence — WebSearch/WebFetch were intermittently returning 502 and I could not fetch the font repos before this output.

research.caveats: Coverage gaps and things that would change the answer: (1) Persian LLM quality evidence for 2026 — I did NOT obtain live benchmark numbers (ParsBench/PersianBench or vendor evals); any model recommendation must be re-verified with a human-eval set of ~50 Persian religious questions. Known risk to test: Arabic-script tokenization inflates token counts and can truncate prompts, and mixed RTL/LTR prompts can cause bidi ordering artifacts in streamed output. (2) RTL font performance (WOFF2 file sizes, harakat rendering on low-end Android) was not measured; the font finding is flagged low confidence with no sources. (3) The repo file's provenance is unknown: it is named quran-simple.txt but contains full diacritics including U+0640+U+0670 sequences typical of Tanzil's enhanced/Uthmani-family texts, not Tanzil 'Simple'; re-download the intended Tanzil type and checksum it. (4) Root count differs by method: 1,642 distinct ROOT strings counted from v0.4 vs commonly cited 1,651 roots on corpus.quran.com — confirm which the site uses before publishing a number. (5) Quranic Arabic Corpus licensing (GPL + 'CHANGING IT IS NOT ALLOWED') likely conflicts with redistributing a modified morphology index; legal review needed. (6) WebSearch returned malformed results and WebFetch intermittently 502'd; only URLs listed in findings were successfully fetched. (7) Hazm/Parsivar are Persian-text tools; no single library covers both Persian normalization and Quranic Arabic normalization — the pipeline must be two-stage and language-detected first.
research.recommendation: Build the retrieval layer on quran-search-engine (MIT, TypeScript, 38 stars, pushed 2026-10-07) for its tokenizer/normalization and root/lemma search, fed by a normalized static index built from Tanzil 'Simple Clean' (search copy) + Tanzil Uthmani/enhanced (display copy) + Quranic Arabic Corpus v0.4 morphology (subject to its GPL/no-modification license). Run Persian queries through Hazm 0.12.1 (MIT) with a custom pre-pass that strips ZWNJ and maps Persian digits, then a Quran-specific Arabic normalizer (strip U+064B-U+065F, U+0670, U+0640, U+06D6-U+06ED; fold أإآٱ->ا, ة->ه, ى->ي for the index only). Runner-up: Alfanous (LGPL-3.0, 285 stars) as a drop-in Arabic Quran search backend if you want a Python server rather than a TS library; its normalizer is the cleanest reference implementation but LGPL obligations apply. Avoid applying Parsivar/Hazm defaults or quran-search-engine's final [ء-ي] filter to Persian input — both destroy Persian letters.

research.topic: $0 hosting + vector stack for a public English/Persian Quran RAG chatbot (verified 2026-10-31)

findings.claim: Cloudflare Workers Free caps at 100,000 requests/day, 10 ms CPU per invocation, 128 MB memory, and 50 subrequests; HTTP duration is unlimited and static-asset requests are free.
findings.detail: Free plan (account-wide): 100,000 requests/day; 10 ms CPU per HTTP request (Paid 5 min); 128 MB per isolate; 50 subrequests/request (Paid 10,000); 64 env vars; 64 MiB script; 100 Workers/account; no HTTP duration limit; Cron/DO alarms/Queue consumers max 15 min. Pages Functions are billed as Workers; static-asset requests are free and unlimited. Streaming an LLM response for minutes is fine because network wait is not CPU, but local brute-force over 6,236 x 768 floats will exceed 10 ms.

findings.claim: Cloudflare Pages Free includes unlimited sites, seats, requests, and bandwidth, with 500 builds/month.
findings.detail: 500 builds/month; 1 concurrent build; 20,000 files/deployment; 25 MiB max asset; 100 custom domains; 100 header rules; 2,000 static redirects + 100 dynamic. 'All plans come with unlimited sites, seats, requests, and bandwidth' (subject to CDN terms). Functions requests count against the Workers 100k/day. No card required for Pages Free.

findings.claim: Cloudflare D1 Free includes 5 GB storage, 5 million rows read/day, 100,000 rows written/day, and 10 databases.
findings.detail: Daily limits reset 00:00 UTC. Hitting read/write limits makes queries fail with an error; at 5 GB, inserts/schema changes are blocked until data is deleted. 6,236 verses plus English/Persian translations and a large answer cache fit easily; 12,472 x 1024 float32 embeddings would be ~51 MB if stored as BLOBs. No card required.

findings.claim: Other Cloudflare Free limits: KV 100k reads + 1k writes/day and 1 GB; R2 10 GB-month + 1M Class A + 10M Class B with free egress; Queues 10k operations/day with 24 h retention; Hyperdrive 100k queries/day.
findings.detail: KV also 1,000 deletes/day, 1,000 list/day, 1,000 namespaces; exceeding a KV limit fails that operation type. R2 free tier is Standard-only; R2 requires an R2 subscription via checkout, so it may not be zero-card. A Queue operation is each 64 KB written/read/deleted; delivery normally costs 3 ops/message; 10,000 queues. Hyperdrive is included in Workers Free: 100,000 database statements/day, then errors.

findings.claim: Cloudflare Vectorize Free allows 30M queried vector dimensions/month, 5M stored vector dimensions, and 100 indexes; 6,236 x 1024-dim vectors do NOT fit (6.39M stored dims > 5M), while 6,236 x 768 fits (4.789M).
findings.detail: Max 1,536 dims/vector; 20M vectors/index; 10 KiB metadata/vector; topK 50 with metadata (100 without). Billing formula counts (queried vectors + stored vectors) x dimensions; docs example: 10,000 vectors at 384 dims + 100 queries = 3.878M queried dims. At 768 dims: 4,789,248 stored, leaving 210,752 dims of storage headroom; (30M - 4.789M)/768 = ~32,826 queries/month (~1,094/day). If stored dims are a separate allowance, 30M/768 = 39,062 queries/month (~1,302/day). 12,472 x 1024 = 12.77M dims, 2.55x the cap. Free-tier overage behavior is not documented; only Paid overage is ($0.01/M queried dims, $0.05/100M stored dims).

findings.claim: Cloudflare Workers AI Free gives 10,000 neurons/day, resets 00:00 UTC, and further operations fail when exhausted; paid overage is $0.011 per 1,000 neurons.
findings.detail: Per M tokens (input/output): @cf/qwen/qwen3-30b-a3b-fp8 4,625/30,475; @cf/google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-it 9,091/27,273; @cf/meta/llama-3.2-3b-instruct 4,625/30,475; @cf/baai/bge-m3 embeddings 1,075/M input at 1024 dims. At ~1,000 input + 250 output tokens, qwen3-30b costs ~12.2 neurons/answer -> ~800 answers/day; at 1,500 + 300 -> ~16.1 -> ~620/day. Indexing 6,236 verses at ~40 tokens/verse with bge-m3 = ~249k tokens = ~268 neurons one-time. @cf/google/embeddinggemma-300m is 768-d (standard size; model card is gated), 100+ languages, listed at $0.0118/M input tokens. Persian output quality is not benchmarked on the Cloudflare pages.

findings.claim: Cloudflare Free gives one IP rate-limiting rule (10 s window, 10 s mitigation), free Turnstile (20 widgets, unlimited challenges), free Durable Objects (100k req/day, 13k GB-s/day), and AI Gateway global rate limiting; KV is unsuitable for token buckets at 1,000 writes/day.
findings.detail: WAF Free: Free Managed Ruleset + custom rules + 1 rate-limiting rule; the rule counts by IP over 10 s and blocks for 10 s. Turnstile Free: up to 20 widgets, 10 hostnames/widget, unlimited challenges; verify the token server-side. DO Free: SQLite-backed only; 100k requests/day; 13,000 GB-s/day; 5M row reads/100k row writes/5 GB. KV Free: 100k reads/day but only 1,000 writes/day and eventual consistency, so a per-request token bucket exhausts writes; use DO SQLite or D1 (100k writes/day). AI Gateway rate limiting is per-gateway global (fixed/sliding, returns 429), a cost circuit breaker, not per-IP. Bot Fight Mode is free but only known-bot signatures, cannot be customized/skipped, and may challenge legitimate API clients; combine Turnstile + the one rate-limit rule + a DO/D1 per-IP daily quota.

findings.claim: Cloudflare's self-serve terms have no Workers-specific non-commercial clause; they ban 'virtual private network or other similar proxy services' (2.2.1(j)) and resale (2.2.1(a)), but an app-specific backend calling an LLM API is not a VPN/proxy service.
findings.detail: The Self-Serve Subscription Agreement does not restrict Free Services to personal/non-commercial use and does not ban non-HTML content for Workers. 2.2.1(j) targets VPN/proxy services; 2.2.1(a) bans renting/leasing/loaning/selling access. There is no explicit safe harbor for LLM API proxying. Technically Workers Free allows 50 subrequests/request and 100k requests/day, and there are no egress charges, so a Worker can stream from a third-party LLM. Confirm with Cloudflare if the site becomes high-volume.

findings.claim: Vercel Hobby is $0 with 1M function invocations, 4 CPU-hours, 360 GB-hours, 100 GB fast data transfer, and 300 s max duration; it is non-commercial personal use only and cannot buy overage.
findings.detail: Hobby also includes 1M CDN requests, 10 GB fast origin transfer, 100 deployments/day, 5,000 image transformations, 50k analytics events. Overages: wait until the 30-day cycle resets; no purchase option. Fair-use text: 'Hobby teams are restricted to non-commercial personal use only. All commercial usage ... requires Pro or Enterprise'; donations do not count as commercial. No credit card needed for Hobby. Good fit for a free, ad-free Quran site; not for ads/paid services.

findings.claim: Netlify Free is 300 credits/month with a hard limit and no auto-recharge; Netlify states 'You'll never be charged for the Free plan.'
findings.detail: New accounts since 2025-09-04 use credit plans. Costs: 15 credits/production deploy, 10 credits/GB-hour compute, 20 credits/GB bandwidth, 2 credits/10,000 web requests. All 300 credits on bandwidth = 15 GB; on requests = 1.5M; on compute = 30 GB-hours; on deploys = 20. Hard limit means metered usage stops at zero until the next cycle; no card or auto-recharge. Legacy pre-2025-09-04 accounts keep old plans.

findings.claim: GitHub Pages free static hosting caps at 1 GB site size, 100 GB/month bandwidth, and 10 builds/hour, and prohibits commercial business/e-commerce/SaaS use.
findings.detail: Source repo recommended <=1 GB; published site <=1 GB; 100 GB/month soft bandwidth; 10 builds/hour (custom Actions exempt). Policy: not to be used as free web hosting for online business, e-commerce, SaaS, or sensitive transactions; a free non-commercial Quran site is allowed. Static only - no server-side API, so pair with Cloudflare Workers for chat/vector/LLM.

findings.claim: Supabase Free gives 500 MB database (shared CPU, 500 MB RAM), 1 GB file storage, 5 GB egress, 50k MAU, and 2 active projects; free projects pause after 7 days of inactivity but restore for up to 1 year.
findings.detail: No automatic backups on Free. pgvector is available (create extension vector), HNSW/IVFFlat; 6,236 x 1024 float32 = ~25.5 MB plus index fits in 500 MB; a cache table also fits. A few DB requests/day prevent pausing. Exceeding 500 MB/egress restricts the project; no paid overage on Free. Free signup does not require a card (not explicitly re-verified).

findings.claim: Neon Free gives 1 GB storage/project (20 GB/account), 100 CU-hours/project/month, 10 branches, 100 projects, 5-minute autosuspend, and no credit card.
findings.detail: Restore window 6 hours (1 GB). pgvector available on every plan; max 2,000 dims for vector (4,000 halfvec), HNSW/IVFFlat. 6,236 x 1024 = ~25.5 MB fits. 100 CU-hours is the real cap: at the 0.25 CU minimum, 400 active hours (~16.7 days at 24/7); if traffic keeps compute awake, it suspends until next cycle, with no bill. Autosuspend after 5 minutes keeps idle usage near zero. 'no credit card required'.

findings.claim: Turso Free includes 100 databases, 5 GB storage, 500M rows read/month, 10M rows written/month, 3 GB syncs, and 1-day PITR, with no credit card; it has native vector search and vector indexes.
findings.detail: Vector types FLOAT64/FLOAT32/FLOAT16/BFLOAT16/FLOAT8/FLOAT1BIT; functions vector_distance_cos, libsql_vector_idx, vector_top_k. 6,236 x 1024 float32 = ~25.5 MB, fits 5 GB; one DB can hold verses, embeddings, and cached answers. Quota failures return BLOCKED, not a bill. Inactive groups can be archived (exact threshold not found). 'Start free, no credit card required'.

findings.claim: Upstash Vector Free includes 200M vector x dimension capacity, 1 GB data, 10,000 query/update operations per day, 100 namespaces, 1,536 max dimensions, and 10 indexes.
findings.detail: Vector storage = vectors x dimensions x 4 bytes; metadata up to 48 KB/vector; data up to 1 MB/vector. 6,236 x 1024 = 6.39M vector-dims (3.2% of 200M) and ~25.5 MB, well under 1 GB; 12,472 x 1024 = 12.77M, also fine. Query/fetch/range count as one op per request regardless of returned vectors; upserts/deletes count per vector. Paid: $0.40/100k requests, $0.25/GB storage. Free max dim 1,536. No card stated; Upstash free tiers normally do not require one.

findings.claim: Qdrant Cloud Free is 0.5 vCPU/1 GB RAM/4 GB disk and free forever but suspends after 1 week and deletes after 4 weeks of inactivity; Pinecone Starter Free is 2 GB storage/5 indexes/2M write units/1M read units per month; MongoDB Atlas M0 is 512 MB and reportedly supports Atlas Vector Search.
findings.detail: Qdrant: single node; 6,236 x 1024 = ~25.5 MB fits; no daily query cap documented; card requirement not stated. Pinecone: 100 namespaces/index, 1 GB egress; 1 read unit per GB of namespace per query with 0.25 RU minimum -> a 25.5 MB namespace costs 0.25 RU/query, so 1M RU = ~4M queries/month. Atlas M0: 512 MB storage, shared; MongoDB docs/search summary says Vector Search is available on M0 with ~3 indexes, but mongodb.com returned HTTP 403 so this is not primary-verified. None of these is needed for the zero-card Cloudflare-only stack.

findings.claim: Hugging Face Spaces no longer offers free Docker/Gradio compute to new free accounts: creating a Gradio or Docker Space requires a paid plan (PRO $9/month); free accounts can host up to 2 Gradio Spaces on ZeroGPU; static Spaces remain free.
findings.detail: Spaces docs: CPU Basic hardware is 2 vCPU/16 GB/50 GB disk with no hourly cost, but 'creating a Space that runs on compute (Gradio or Docker) requires a paid plan' (PRO for personal, Team/Enterprise for orgs); free personal accounts in good standing can host up to 2 Gradio Spaces on ZeroGPU. Pricing page lists CPU Basic and ZeroGPU as FREE and PRO ($9/month) as 'Host ZeroGPU, Gradio & Docker Spaces' - a contradiction; the docs are more specific. Free hardware sleeps after inactivity. Not suitable for an always-on RAG API/vector DB.

findings.claim: Render Free is 0.1 CPU/512 MB with 750 instance-hours/month and 15-minute spin-down; it can bill bandwidth overage if a card is on file and may suspend services that make many external API calls. Fly.io has no free tier (smallest always-on VM $2.19/30 days); Railway has no recurring free tier (one-time ~$5 trial).
findings.detail: Render: 750 hours/workspace/month; idle services do not consume hours; ~1 minute cold start; ephemeral filesystem; free Postgres 1 GB expires 30 days after creation (14-day grace). If outbound bandwidth is exhausted, Render bills a supplementary amount when a payment method exists, otherwise suspends free services; service-initiated traffic (external DB/API calls) can trigger suspension - bad for an LLM proxy. Fly: bills by the second, no monthly platform fee, 2 VM-hours or 7-day free trial then payment method. Railway: pricing page unreachable from this network (connection refused); established baseline is no recurring free plan, one-time $5 trial, Hobby ~$5/month; verify live before relying.

research.caveats: Not verified: Railway pricing page (connection refused; $5 trial/Hobby $5 is baseline, not live); MongoDB Atlas pages (HTTP 403; 512 MB and Vector Search on M0 come from a search summary, not a primary page); Pinecone/Qdrant/Supabase card requirements are not explicitly documented; Cloudflare Vectorize free-tier overage behavior beyond the allocation (docs only describe Paid billing); Cloudflare R2 activation may require a card via checkout; Upstash Vector/Turso inactivity deletion thresholds; Persian output quality of Workers AI models is not benchmarked. Free-tier terms change frequently. Vectorize math assumes billing counts stored+queried dimensions as the docs' formula states; if stored and queried are separate allowances, the ceiling is ~39k queries/month instead of ~33k. A 1024-dim Vectorize index is impossible on Free either way. Cloudflare Workers AI model ids/prices are current as of the 2026-10-31 fetch and may change. The legal reading of Cloudflare's proxy clause is an interpretation, not a Cloudflare statement. What would change the answer: a higher Vectorize stored-dimension cap, a Workers AI neuron increase, accepting a $5/month paid tier (Workers Paid/Fly/Railway), or a Persian-quality requirement that forces bge-m3 1024-d vectors and therefore an external vector DB.
research.recommendation: Primary ($0, no credit card): Cloudflare Pages (static EN/FA UI, RTL) + Workers Free (chat API/SSE proxy) + D1 (6,236 Arabic verses + English/Persian translations + cached answers) + Vectorize Free + Workers AI Free + Turnstile + the one free WAF rate-limit rule + AI Gateway cache/global cap. Use ONE multilingual 768-d index with @cf/google/embeddinggemma-300m: 6,236 x 768 = 4,789,248 stored dims, under the 5M cap, leaving ~33k-39k vector queries/month (~1.1k-1.3k/day). Generate with @cf/qwen/qwen3-30b-a3b-fp8 (4,625 input / 30,475 output neurons per M tokens): at ~1,000 input + 250 output tokens that is ~12.2 neurons/answer, so ~800 answers/day under the 10k neurons/day free allowance; at 1,500+300 it is ~620/day. Cache answers in D1 before embedding/generation to stretch both quotas. This stack has hard caps, no card, no surprise bill, and no non-commercial clause. It cannot store 1024-d vectors (6,385,664 dims > 5M) or 12k vectors, and 1024-d Vectorize is the hard blocker. Runner-up ($0, no card): the same Cloudflare front end + Upstash Vector Free (1 GB, 10,000 query/update ops/day, 1,536 dims) with @cf/baai/bge-m3 1024-d embeddings (6,236 x 1024 = 6.39M vector-dims, 3.2% of the 200M vector x dimension cap), plus D1 or Turso Free for text/cache. This removes the 768-d/5M-dim constraint and raises retrieval to 10k queries/day at the cost of a second vendor; Workers AI's 10k neurons/day remains the answer-rate bottleneck. Single-DB alternative: Turso Free (5 GB, native vector index, 500M rows read/month, no card) can hold verses + vectors + cache, with 1024-d FLOAT32 embeddings at ~25.5 MB.

research.topic: Quran/Islamic QA and RAG prior art for a free, Quran-only, English+Persian public chatbot (verified 2026-10-31)

findings.claim: QRCD (Quran Reading Comprehension Dataset) is the core Arabic extractive Quran QA benchmark: v1.1 has 1,093 question-passage pairs / 1,337 question-passage-answer triplets; v1.2 adds 62 unanswerable pairs.
findings.detail: v1.1 splits 819 train QP (989 QPA) and 274 test QP (348 QPA), in SQuAD v1.1 JSON format, built on Tanzil simple-clean 1.0.2 text. v1.2 keeps the 1,093 and adds 62 QP pairs whose questions have no answer in the passage. License: dataset CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; code and CL-AraBERT model Apache-2.0 (the LICENSE heading says 'CC-BY-ND' but the body says CC BY-NC-ND 4.0). Reuse: Arabic-only evaluation, especially the 62 no-answer items for refusal testing; NC-ND means use as a test set, not for training or modified redistribution.

findings.claim: tarteel-ai/quranqa is AyaTEC, not QRCD: 207 Arabic questions, 1,762 annotated answers, 11 topic categories; AyaTEC v1.2 passage retrieval has 251 questions / 1,599 QP pairs including 37 zero-answer questions.
findings.detail: AyaTEC is a 2020 ACM TALLIP reusable test collection (DOI 10.1145/3400396); the HF card was last modified 2024-09-11. v1.2 PR split: 174 train questions / 972 QP, 25 dev / 160 QP, 52 test / 427 QP; 37 zero-answer questions (~15%). License: CC-BY-ND 4.0. Reuse: Arabic eval set and an 11-category topic taxonomy for a concept layer; zero-answer subset for refusal; ND blocks derivative redistribution.

findings.claim: The Quranic Arabic Corpus annotates all 6,236 verses with morphology, a dependency treebank and a concept ontology, and is licensed GPLv3.
findings.detail: Version 0.4; roughly 77,000 word-level annotations; Word-by-Word grammar, syntactic treebank, semantic ontology, Java API and downloadable morphology/treebank files. The license page reproduces GNU GPL Version 3, 29 June 2007.
