Reuse: word-by-word grammar and an ontology/topic layer; it is copyleft, so isolate it or open-source derivatives, and underlying translation rights are separate.

findings.claim: ArabicMMLU contains 2,222 Islamic Studies rows across four configs inside a 14,575-question / 40-task Arabic benchmark; license CC-BY-NC-4.0.
findings.detail: Config row counts: Islamic Studies 642; Islamic Studies (Primary School) 1,002; (Middle School) 241; (High School) 337; overall 14,575 multiple-choice questions. Reuse: Arabic knowledge/Islamic-studies evaluation only; it is not Quran-only, has no Persian, and is non-commercial.

findings.claim: IslamicFaithQA is a 3,810-item bilingual Arabic/English generative benchmark built to measure hallucination and abstention, released Apache-2.0.
findings.detail: Atomic single-gold answers; the paper also releases 25K Arabic text-grounded SFT reasoning pairs, 5K bilingual preference samples, and a ~6k verse retrieval corpus. Reuse: directly as English/Arabic refusal and abstention evaluation, and as SFT data; no Persian.

findings.claim: QuranicMMLU (Sep 2026) is a 980-question human-reviewed benchmark of Quranic Arabic linguistic knowledge with both open-ended and multiple-choice items.
findings.detail: Five-pillar taxonomy: phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics, pragmatics. Models score higher on MCQ accuracy than open-ended answer quality. No dataset URL or license is stated in the arXiv abstract, so reuse depends on locating a released, licensed copy.

findings.claim: Open tafsir QA data is Arabic/English-only: Mofaser has 243,129 QA records over 6,236 verses from 18 tafsirs under CC-BY-4.0; a 2024 benchmark offers 73,000+ tafsir/hadith QA pairs.
findings.detail: Mofaser: 8 Arabic + 10 English classical tafsir sources, formatted as verse-plus-explanation QA. The 73k dataset covers Quranic tafsir and ahadith with contextual enrichment; its paper reports ROUGE-vs-human verdict consistency of only 11-20%, so automatic metrics are unreliable. tarteel-ai/quran-tafsir (6,236 rows, five English translations) has no license and is not safely reusable. Reuse: filter to Quran-only, fine-tune or evaluate; no Persian.

findings.claim: quran-mcp (120 stars, Python) is a turnkey MCP server over quran.com data: 50+ translations in 30+ languages, 15+ tafsirs, search and morphology, under QFGPL-1.0.
findings.detail: Docker Compose + Postgres; Arabic in Hafs/Warsh/Qaloon; tafsir from Ibn Kathir, Tabari, Qurtubi, Sa'di and others; mushaf rendering. QFGPL-1.0 (March 2026) is non-commercial, network-copyleft, credit-required and software-only. Reuse: strongest backend for a free non-commercial site if you will open-source the service; Quran data licenses are separate.

findings.claim: tafsir-mcp (73 stars) exposes 13 tools over 6,236 ayahs, 77,432 words, 1,891 roots and five classical tafsirs; code is MIT and data CC BY 4.0.
findings.detail: Tools include fetch_ayah, fetch_tafsir, search_quran_text, analyze_word and get_qeraat_variants. Tafsirs: Tabari, Ibn Kathir, Baghawi, Saadi, Muyassar, plus trilingual Mukhtasar (Arabic/English/Bengali). Reuse: direct ingestion with attribution to the Tafsir Center for Quranic Studies; no Persian tafsir.

findings.claim: Alfanous (285 stars, LGPL-3.0) is the mature Arabic Quran search engine; QuranAnalysis (104 stars) adds semantic search, ontology and QA but has no license.
findings.detail: Alfanous: Boolean/Buckwalter queries, faceted search by sura/juz/topic, Python library plus REST, Arabic-only. QuranAnalysis: 20,000+ lines of code, ontology, semantic search and question answering from a Leeds MSc project; GitHub reports no license, so the code is not legally reusable. Reuse: Alfanous search/index concepts under LGPL; QuranAnalysis ideas only.

findings.claim: QuranHub API provides 550+ editions in 90+ languages under a non-commercial license; quran_android is GPL-3.0 (2,426 stars), while quran.com-frontend-next (1,928 stars) has no license.
findings.detail: QuranHub's NCL permits use, copy, modification and distribution for non-commercial purposes only. quran_android is a Kotlin reading app. quran.com-frontend-next is TypeScript/Next.js and GitHub reports no license, so it is reference-only. Reuse: self-host QuranHub if NCL fits; GPL obligations apply to Android code; do not copy the frontend.

findings.claim: Quran Foundation's quran.ai implements a Read-Select-Ask-Discover loop inside ChatGPT/Claude with 20 tafsir editions, 31 translations in 12 languages and mandatory citations.
findings.detail: Grounding rules require citations, preserve scholarly differences and distinguish retrieved commentary from AI synthesis; answers link cited ayahs back into the mushaf, sourced from quran.com/Quran Foundation. quran.com's own public homepage still shows reading/listening/study with no AI chatbot. Reuse: strongest UX and grounding blueprint; the 12 languages are not enumerated, so Persian support is unverified.

findings.claim: Tarteel is a recitation/memorization AI, not a Quran QA chatbot; it claims 15M+ users and charges $12.99/month or $89.99/year for Premium.
findings.detail: Core interaction: hide verses, recite from memory, get word-level mistake detection and live correction. US App Store: 4.72 stars / 11,018 ratings. The live pricing payload stores 1299 and 8999 USD cents, while JSON-LD on the same page also lists $9.99/month and $90/year, so the price is internally inconsistent. Reuse: voice-recitation interaction pattern only.

findings.claim: Ayah Finder is a retrieval-only AI Quran search app: natural-language queries by feeling, topic, situation or verse reference in any language; free, no ads, 50K+ downloads claimed.
findings.detail: The app explicitly says it 'will never generate any content' and uses a Quran database plus translations and tafsirs. The website claims a 4.8 rating and 50K+ downloads; the US App Store listing fetched on 2026-10-31 showed 0 ratings, so marketing metrics are unverified. Reuse: best refusal-first, citation-only UX model.

findings.claim: Muslim Pro's Ask AiDeen is a Quran+hadith chatbot capped at three questions per session for free users; Quranly is a habit/streak app with no QA.
findings.detail: Ask AiDeen launched in Ramadan 2025 (article updated 2025-09-27), was built with Google's Data Science team, unlocks unlimited questions with premium, and carries a not-a-fatwa disclaimer. Muslim Pro: 4.70 stars / 600,669 US ratings. Quranly: 4.71 / 1,651 ratings, reading goals and streaks, no AI assistant. Reuse: freemium question cap and habit loop; neither is Quran-only.

findings.claim: The leading Persian Quran app, قرآن هادی (Hadi App), is a reading/tafsir app with 4.86 stars / 78,743 US ratings and no AI Q&A.
findings.detail: Free app: full mushaf, Persian translation, Tafsir al-Mizan, Tafsir Nemuneh, Tafsir Noor and Tafsir Ahl al-Bayt, multiple reciters, Persian+English word-by-word, and audio tafsir. Other Persian apps (Zekr Quran, Tafsir Farsi Kalemeh) are similar reading/tafsir products. Reuse: feature baseline for the Persian UI; confirms there is no dominant Persian Quran chatbot.

findings.claim: FARSIQA is the only 2025 Persian Islamic RAG system found; it reports 97.0% negative rejection and 74.3% answer correctness on IslamicPCQA, but releases no code or data.
findings.detail: Knowledge base: 1M+ authoritative Islamic documents; FAIR-RAG decomposes queries and iterates retrieval for multi-hop questions. IslamicPCQA: 12,282 Persian multi-hop QA pairs from nine Islamic encyclopedias, not Quran-only; no Hugging Face or GitHub release found. Reuse: negative-rejection metric and benchmark design only.

findings.claim: Persian Quran content is thin in open APIs: quran.com has 20 tafsirs but zero Persian, and 126 translations but only two Persian; AlQuran.cloud and Tanzil each list 13 Persian text translations.
findings.detail: quran.com tafsir languages are Arabic, English, Bengali, Urdu, Russian and Kurdish. Persian translations on quran.com are IslamHouse.com (id 135) and Hussein Taji Kal Dari (id 29). Tanzil translations are non-commercial only and require a backlink if more than three are used; Tanzil Arabic text is verbatim-only with attribution and a backlink. Reuse: ingest two or three Persian translations; Persian tafsir must be sourced and licensed separately.

findings.claim: No Persian Quran-only QA/eval set or Persian refusal benchmark was found; refusal coverage is Arabic zero-answer sets plus an Arabic/English abstention benchmark.
findings.detail: Available refusal/abstention data: QRCD v1.2 (62 no-answer QP), AyaTEC v1.2 (37 zero-answer questions) and IslamicFaithQA (3,810 Arabic/English items). No English-Persian parallel query/verse set was found. Concept-layer options: QuranAnalysis ontology (no license) or nazimali/quran-question-answer-context (CC-BY-4.0, Arabic/English, q_topic and ontology_concept fields). Build: 300-500 Persian Quran-only questions with unanswerable/out-of-scope items plus a bilingual concept index.

findings.claim: Reported 2025-2026 Arabic Quranic QA results converge on hybrid retrieval + cross-encoder reranking + LLM span extraction, with MAP@10 around 0.31-0.49 depending on the split.
findings.detail: Two-Stage ensemble on Quran QA 2023: MAP@10 0.3128, MRR@10 0.5763, pAP@10 0.669. Hybrid Neural Retrieval on expanded Qur'an QA 2022: Recall@10 0.7024, MAP@10 0.4947, MRR 0.5807. Few-shot instruction-tuned LLMs: pAP10 0.637. Fanar-Sadiq adds multi-agent intent routing, exact verse lookup with quotation validation, and citation-normalized fiqh answers. Reuse: retrieval/rerank/extract pipeline plus quotation validation for refusal.

research.caveats: WebSearch returned non-live, sometimes fabricated summaries in this session; every fact above was instead verified by direct HTTP fetch of primary pages/APIs on 2026-10-31 (Hugging Face API, GitHub API, ACL Anthology, arXiv API, official product sites, iTunes Search API). GitLab blocked access (HTTP 1009), so QRCD v1.2 file-level licensing was inferred from the v1.1 repo and v1.2 counts come from the ACL 2023 paper. 'No Persian X found' claims are bounded by Hugging Face/GitHub/API searches, not a global census. quran.ai's 12 languages are not enumerated, so Persian support is unverified. Tarteel's price is internally inconsistent ($12.99/$89.99 live payload vs $9.99/$90 JSON-LD). User-uploaded CC licenses (Mofaser, nazimali) may not clear underlying tafsir/translation rights. Star counts and app ratings are 2026-10-31 snapshots.
research.recommendation: Pick: build a thin, citation-first bilingual RAG with quran.ai's Read-Select-Ask-Discover UX, over Tanzil Arabic (verbatim, attributed), 2-3 Persian translations from Tanzil/AlQuran.cloud under their non-commercial terms, and tafsir-mcp's CC-BY-4.0 Arabic/English tafsir data; add a separately licensed Persian tafsir corpus (none exists in open APIs) and a 300-500-item Persian Quran-only eval with unanswerable/out-of-scope items. Evaluate Arabic/English with QRCD v1.2, AyaTEC v1.2 and IslamicFaithQA, especially their no-answer/abstention subsets. Runner-up: fork quran-mcp (QFGPL-1.0) as the backend if fully open-sourcing the service is acceptable.

research.topic: Product-trust design for a free, bilingual (English/Persian) Quran Q&A chatbot: answer format, religious-authority boundaries, translation policy, sensitive-topic handling, and a concrete answer contract

findings.claim: Egypt's Dar al-Ifta ruled in January 2026 that using AI independently to interpret the Quran is religiously impermissible.
findings.detail: Grand Mufti Nazir Ayyad, through Dar Al Ifta Al Misriyyah, ruled that relying independently or entirely on AI applications including ChatGPT for Quranic interpretation is "not permissible" / "prohibited under Islamic law". Stated reasons: AI lacks true comprehension, works by automated data processing, and exposes the Quran to "conjecture, inaccuracies and misrepresentation". Muslims are directed to authentic tafsir works, qualified scholars, and accredited institutions. Date reported as 27 Jan 2026 by Gulf News and 28 Jan 2026 by IQNA.

findings.claim: Quran Foundation's API terms require Quranic snippets to preserve their original context and meaning and forbid arranging them in ways that alter or misrepresent the Quran's intended message.
findings.detail: Developer Terms last updated 2026-10-11, section 2.2: the text of the Quran must be "not modified in any way"; snippets must be "presented in a manner that preserves their original context and meaning", and the developer "may not arrange or display snippets in a way that alters or misrepresents the intended message of the source material". QF Content must never be used in a context that promotes hate, extremism, or misinformation. A public Privacy Policy and Terms of Use are mandatory.

findings.claim: Quran Foundation permits commercial/freemium use and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) of its content, but caps ordinary API-content caching at one week.
findings.detail: Section 2.2 allows charging for an app, subscriptions, ads, donations, and freemium use without a separate commercial license, provided QF Content is only part of the end-user experience and is not sold, sublicensed, or redistributed as data. Section 3.1: do not cache or store QF Content longer than 1 week unless using Content Sync, which must be re-synced at least every 7 days. "AI and retrieval use": RAG within the application is distinct from training a model; retained content and embeddings remain subject to storage and use restrictions.

findings.claim: Quran Foundation explicitly warns against machine-translating Quran text returned by its API.
findings.detail: QF API FAQ: "The API already delivers peer-reviewed translations. Auto-translating them can distort meaning and create theological inaccuracies." It instructs developers to disable automatic translation of Quran text using HTML/CSP techniques. This means the Persian UI must use a vetted Persian translation edition, not runtime translation of English or Arabic.

findings.claim: Quran.com's verse page displays Arabic word-by-word, a translator-attributed English translation with numbered footnotes, and author-labelled tafsir, but no fatwa disclaimer is visible on the verse page.
findings.detail: On quran.com/2/255: breadcrumb "Al-Baqarah", reference "2:255", Arabic word-by-word layout, English translation with superscript footnotes (e.g. "His Seat¹"), buttons "Continue Reading", "Read Tafsir", "View Tafsirs"; tafsir preview headed "Ibn Kathir (Abridged)"; a "Notes and Reflections" section. No fatwa/religious-advice disclaimer appeared in the page content.

findings.claim: Quran.com's translation catalog exposes 8 English translations plus transliteration but only 2 Persian translations.
findings.detail: English ids: 20 Saheeh International; 19 M. Pickthall; 22 A. Yusuf Ali; 85 M.A.S. Abdel Haleem; 84 T. Usmani; 95 A. Maududi (Tafhim commentary); 149 Fadel Soliman, Bridges' translation; 203 Al-Hilali & Khan; 57 Transliteration. Persian: 135 IslamHouse.com and 29 Hussein Taji Kal Dari (slug oddly "fr-hussein-taji"). No Persian tafsir is listed.

findings.claim: The wider AlQuran.cloud catalog offers 17 English and 13 Persian translation editions, showing that Persian coverage is much richer outside Quran.com.
findings.detail: Persian edition ids: fa.ayati (آیتی), fa.fooladvand (فولادوند), fa.ghomshei (الهی قمشه‌ای), fa.makarem (مکارم شیرازی), fa.ansarian (انصاریان), fa.bahrampour (بهرام پور), fa.khorramshahi (خرمشاهی), fa.mojtabavi (مجتبوی), fa.khorramdel (خرمدل), fa.moezzi (معزی), fa.gharaati (قرائتی), fa.sadeqi (صادقی تهرانی), fa.safavi (صفوی). English includes en.sahih (Saheeh International), en.pickthall, en.yusufali, en.haleem? (not listed; alquran.cloud list has 17 including en.ahmedali, en.arberry, en.asad, en.daryabadi, en.hilali, en.sahih, en.sarwar, en.yusufali, en.maududi, en.shakir, en.itani, en.mubarakpuri, en.qarai, en.wahiduddin, en.qaribullah, en.ahmedraza).

findings.claim: Tanzil's translation repository is licensed for non-commercial use only and requires a link back when more than three translations are used in a website or app.
findings.detail: Tanzil states translations are for "non-commercial purposes only"; if more than three translations are used, a link back to its translations page is required; redistributing its translation list in another website is not allowed without direct permission. Tanzil's developer FAQ also says resources "are available for non-commercial purposes". Tanzil lists 13 Persian translations (Ansarian, Ayati, Bahrampour, Gharaati, Ghomshei, Khorramdel, Khorramshahi, Sadeqi Tehrani, Safavi, Fooladvand, Mojtabavi, Moezzi, Makarem Shirazi) and 17 English.

findings.claim: Quran.com's API contains only three English tafsir works and zero Persian tafsir works, leaving a Persian tafsir gap for a bilingual product.
findings.detail: Tafsir resources: 169 Ibn Kathir (Abridged), Hafiz Ibn Kathir, English, slug en-tafisr-ibn-kathir; 168 Ma'arif al-Qur'an, Mufti Muhammad Shafi, English; 817 Tazkirul Quran (Maulana Wahiduddin Khan), English. No Persian-language tafsir entry was returned. A Persian UI must either omit tafsir, show an English tafsir with a clear language label, or license a Persian tafsir separately (e.g. Tafsir Nemuneh by Makarem Shirazi) — each has copyright implications.

findings.claim: Ansari, a retrieval-grounded Islamic AI assistant, answers only from retrieved Islamic corpora with citations; its published validation reports 65% of Ansari 3.0 answers containing citations to authentic Islamic sources.
findings.detail: arXiv abstract: "agentic retrieval loop" searches authenticated corpora (Qur'an, hadith, fiqh, tafsir) and "answers only on the basis of what it retrieves, with citations attached for verification"; noted for "strongly resisting false premises". Validation page: BATIK v1 100-question benchmark, Ansari 3.0 "100% accuracy", "65% of answers now contain citations to authentic Islamic sources"; FAQ says RAG tools "significantly reduce hallucination" and the assistant is constrained to Islam-related topics.

findings.claim: Quran Ayah Finder is an AI semantic-search app that returns matched verses with translation, tafsir and related topics, claiming 15 translations, 8 tafsirs and 6 languages, with no visible fatwa disclaimer.
findings.detail: Homepage: "Describe your problem, feeling, or verse number in any language — our app finds the exact Quranic solution"; search result card shows Arabic verse, English translation, "View Related Topics"; "15 Translations, 8 Tafsirs, 6 Languages, 5 Arabic Fonts"; "100% free, no ads"; footer links FAQ/Privacy/Terms but no fatwa or scholarly-review statement visible. This is the closest product model to a retrieval-first Quran answer bot.

findings.claim: A fatwa is a legal ruling by a qualified mufti in response to a specific question and is generally non-binding in Sunni Islam, while tafsir is Quranic exegesis by a mufassir.
findings.detail: Fatwa: "legal ruling on a point of Islamic law (sharia) delivered by a qualified legal scholar, called a mufti, in answer to a specific question from an individual, judge, or government body"; normally nonbinding unless issued by a government judge in an Islamic state (Shia marja' rulings are treated as binding by followers). Tafsir: "exegesis, or commentary, of the Quran"; author is a mufassir; attempts to provide explanation, interpretation, context or commentary. Implication: an AI answer must never be labelled a fatwa, and even a tafsir excerpt is a named scholar's interpretation, not the Quran's own voice.

findings.claim: Quran Foundation's Answers API models Q&A as ayah-linked records with question type, verse ranges, references and answeredBy attribution, and falls back to English for non-Arabic languages.
findings.detail: GET answers for a specific ayah returns questions with `type` in {CLARIFICATION, TAFSIR, COMMUNITY}, `ranges` (e.g. 2:255-2:257), `references` (e.g. "Tafsir al-Tabari"), `summary`, `theme`, `language`, and `answers[]` with `body`, `answeredBy`, `status`, `language`. Documentation states: "Non-Arabic languages resolve to English upstream" and `ar` returns Arabic; every other language returns English. This is a ready-made schema for answer cards, but it offers no Persian Q&A content.

findings.claim: Stable verse deep links can be formed as quran.com/<surah>/<ayah> and tanzil.net/#<surah>:<ayah>, with Tanzil also supporting translation-specific links.
findings.detail: quran.com/2/255 resolves to Surah Al-Baqarah, ayah 255. Tanzil deep links: http://tanzil.net/#21:4; translation tab: http://tanzil.net/#trans/<transID>/<address>, e.g. http://tanzil.net/#trans/en.shakir/21:4; Quran tab with translation: http://tanzil.net/#quran/en.shakir/21:4. These give every answer a verifiable, clickable citation rather than an opaque claim.

findings.claim: Quran.com's consumer website terms conflict with the Quran Foundation API developer terms: the website restricts content to personal, non-commercial use and bans derivative works, while the API terms allow commercial and freemium applications.
findings.detail: quran.com/terms-and-conditions: content is "FOR YOUR PERSONAL, NON-COMMERCIAL USE ONLY"; users must not use the Service "for any revenue generating endeavor"; users may not "make any modification, adaptation, improvement, enhancement, translation or derivative work." In contrast, api-docs.quran.foundation/legal/developer-terms/ section 2.2 explicitly allows charging for an Application, subscriptions, ads, donations, and freemium models, subject to conditions. A developer must use the API terms for API-served content, not scrape the website, and should obtain legal review of which terms govern.

findings.claim: TIME's May 2026 reporting documents scholarly concerns that Islamic AI tools are built without qualified scholars and that chatbots have produced basic religious errors.
findings.detail: TIME (26 May 2026): Sheikh Kashiff Khan warns AI systems for Islamic knowledge are being built "without sufficient involvement from qualified Islamic scholars"; Waleed Kadous notes ChatGPT once incorrectly told Muslims to wash their knees before prayer; Tarteel's MCP server aims to prevent chatbots from "hallucinate[ing] verses"; Egypt's Dar al-Ifta banned AI Quran interpretation in January 2026. This supports a citation-first, retrieval-only design over free-form generation.

findings.claim: No public usage-share data for Persian Quran translations was found; catalog prevalence points to Ghomshei and Makarem Shirazi as the most widely distributed Persian editions, with Ansarian and Fooladvand as common alternatives.
findings.detail: Each of Tanzil, AlQuran.cloud and Quran.com lists Persian translations, but none publishes user-preference shares. Ghomshei (الهی قمشه‌ای) is the classical literary translation widely printed in Iranian homes; Makarem Shirazi (مکارم شیرازی) is bundled with the widely distributed Tafsir Nemuneh; Ansarian (انصاریان) and Fooladvand (فولادوند) are common in apps and school contexts. Treat default choice as a product hypothesis to validate with Iranian users, not an established fact.

research.caveats: Primary Dar al-Ifta page (dar-alifta.org) refused connection from this environment and IslamWeb/SeekersGuidance blocked curl, so the January 2026 ruling rests on Gulf News, IQNA and TIME secondary reports, with a one-day date discrepancy (27 vs 28 Jan 2026) between outlets. Tarteel's site is JavaScript-only and its terms/FAQ text could not be extracted; the finding that it is a recitation/memorization tool rather than a Q&A/fatwa service is based on search-result titles and the TIME article, not its own documentation. Individual translation copyrights were not verified: Tanzil's compilation is non-commercial-only, but each translator/publisher (e.g. Saheeh International, Makarem Shirazi, Ansarian) may impose additional terms; a public site must clear rights per edition. The Quran Foundation website terms vs API terms conflict needs legal review. The Persian default-translation recommendation is an informed hypothesis, not measured user preference. Quran.com's UI observations are from server-rendered content and may omit controls (audio, share, translation selector) that load client-side. No user testing was done for Persian RTL typography or refusal-copy comprehension.
research.recommendation:
RECOMMENDED DESIGN: a retrieval-only "Verse Card" answer contract — never generate commentary, tafsir, or fatwas. Runner-up: Ansari-style retrieval-grounded generation with mandatory inline citations, acceptable only if every sentence is traceable to a retrieved verse/tafsir and a human scholar reviews outputs; it is higher-risk under Dar al-Ifta's January 2026 ruling.

EXACT ANSWER CONTRACT (JSON fields):
1. request_id: string
2. lang: "en" | "fa"
3. intent: "quran_topic" | "fiqh" | "history" | "personal_guidance" | "off_topic" | "no_retrieval"
4. status: "answered" | "answered_with_boundary" | "refused_off_topic" | "refused_no_retrieval"
5. verses[]: each { surah:int, ayah:int, surah_name_en, surah_name_fa, arabic_tanzil:string (unmodified quran-simple.txt), translations:[{edition_id, translator, language:"en"|"fa", text, license}], context:{ayah_before, ayah_after}, tafsir:[{work_id, work_title, author, translator, language, excerpt, publisher_url}] (optional; only published, attributed works) }
6. citation: { quran_com_url:"https://quran.com/{surah}/{ayah}", tanzil_url:"https://tanzil.net/#{surah}:{ayah}" }
7. disclosure: { arabic_source:"Tanzil quran-simple.txt (Hafs)", translation_not_quran:true, tafsir_is_interpretation:true, not_a_fatwa:true }
8. actions: ["copy_arabic","copy_translation","share_card"]
9. audit: { retrieval_score:float, matched_terms:string[] }
10. generated_commentary: false

UI RULES: Arabic first, then the translation directly beneath with a visible translator label ("Translation: Saheeh International — translation is interpretation, not the Quran"). Second translation collapsed by default; all translations selectable. Tafsir collapsed and labelled by author/work ("Ibn Kathir, Abridged — scholarly interpretation, not a fatwa"). Context panel shows the previous and next ayah. English defaults: Saheeh International (quran.com id 20) primary, M.A.S. Abdel Haleem secondary. Persian defaults: الهی قمشه‌ای (fa.ghomshei) primary, مکارم شیرازی (fa.makarem) secondary; selector exposes all 13 Tanzil Persian editions. Persian UI: RTL, Persian digits, Vazirmatn-style font; Arabic verse visually distinct from Persian translation. No transliteration in the Persian UI; optional in English. NEVER machine-translate a verse at runtime.

INTENT HANDLING:
- quran_topic -> answer with Verse Cards.
- fiqh/legal ("is X haram?") -> status "answered_with_boundary": show only relevant verses, never a ruling; fixed boundary text. Do not infer halal/haram.
- history -> answer only if Quranic verses retrieved; otherwise state the Quran does not provide the detail and point to tafsir/seerah; do not invent.
- personal_guidance -> verses plus open reflection prompts, never counselling or rulings.
- off_topic -> refuse.
- no relevant verse above retrieval threshold -> refuse; never answer from model memory.

REFUSAL COPY (exact):
Off-topic, EN: "I can only answer questions about the Quran. This question is outside that scope, so I cannot answer it."
Off-topic, FA: «من فقط به پرسش‌هایی درباره قرآن پاسخ می‌دهم. این پرسش خارج از این حوزه است و نمی‌توانم به آن پاسخ دهم.»
No retrieval, EN: "I could not find a Quranic verse relevant to this question, so I cannot answer it. Try rephrasing with Quranic terms, or consult a qualified scholar."
No retrieval, FA: «هیچ آیه‌ای از قرآن مرتبط با این پرسش پیدا نکردم؛ بنابراین نمی‌توانم به آن پاسخ دهم. لطفاً پرسش را با واژه‌های قرآنی بازنویسی کنید یا با عالمی واجد شرایط مشورت کنید.»
Fiqh boundary, EN: "The Quran addresses this topic, but a ruling (fatwa) requires a qualified mufti. The relevant verses are shown below; this is not a fatwa."
Fiqh boundary, FA: «قرآن درباره این موضوع آیاتی دارد، اما صدور حکم شرعی (فتوا) فقط از سوی مفتی واجد شرایط ممکن است. آیات مرتبط در ادامه آمده است؛ این پاسخ فتوا نیست.»
Sensitive-verse standing note, EN: "Read in context: the full verse and adjacent verses are shown. Translations and interpretations differ; only the Arabic Quranic text is authoritative."
Sensitive-verse note, FA: «در بافت بخوانید: آیه کامل و آیات مجاور نمایش داده شده است. ترجمه‌ها و تفسیرها متفاوت‌اند؛ تنها متن عربی قرآن مرجع است.»

SENSITIVE TOPICS: always render the complete verse (never a truncated clause), include one ayah before and after, show at least two translations where available, and offer tafsir excerpts from at least two named works when available. Do not add editorial framing, apologies, or "this verse is often misused" commentary generated by AI; instead a neutral fixed context panel with surah, revelation place/period, and adjacent verses. Never label a verse as violent/controversial in the UI taxonomy; index by surah/ayah and topic only. This satisfies Quran Foundation's terms that snippets preserve original context and meaning, and avoids the "conjecture" Dar al-Ifta warned against.

dangerousClaims: Gemini API's free tier is the report's primary $0 provider and was assumed to give ~250 requests/day; all Google pages returned HTTP 403, so the free quota and continued availability are unconfirmed and relying on it could cause outages or a surprise bill.
Cloudflare Workers AI must stop at 10,000 Neurons/day rather than silently billing overage; if that hard cap is wrong, a public site could incur charges.
Groq's report conclusion that it is paid-only is wrong; Groq still has a Free plan at 30 RPM / 1,000 RPD, so excluding it unnecessarily removes a usable $0 fallback.
Alibaba Model Studio automatically switches to pay-as-you-go after the 90-day free quota unless 'Free Quota Only' is explicitly enabled, creating a silent-billing risk.
OpenRouter's 1,000 free requests/day require a one-time $10 purchase and are shared across every end user of the app; the $10 spend and the daily cap are real constraints, not an unlimited free tier.
Cohere trial keys are explicitly not permitted for production or commercial use, so using them for a public site breaches the terms.
Mistral's Free mode is intended for evaluation and prototyping only; using it for a public production site is outside its stated purpose.
NVIDIA NIM endpoints are positioned as prototyping-only; using the free endpoint for production requires a paid NIM container or partner deployment, and the 40 RPM claim could not be verified.

Quran Foundation's Developer Terms prohibit caching QF content longer than one week and prohibit building machine-learning models or embeddings from QF content without written consent, creating legal risk.

Tanzil Quran text may not be modified and requires clear attribution plus a link to tanzil.net; stripping diacritics for indexing is a modification of the distributed text unless the displayed and indexed copies are kept separate.
Tanzil translations are licensed for non-commercial use only; adding ads, sponsorship or a paid tier would breach the terms.

Quran.com's website terms restrict content to personal, non-commercial use and ban derivative works, while the QF API terms allow commercial and freemium use; relying on the wrong terms creates legal exposure.
Egypt's Dar al-Ifta ruled that independent AI interpretation of the Quran is religiously impermissible; a product that generates tafsir or fatwas carries religious and reputational risk.
Cloudflare Vectorize Free stores only 5M vector dimensions, so a 1024-d index for 6,236 verses does not fit; deploying one would require paid capacity or a design change.
Cloudflare Pages Free is capped at 100 projects per account, not unlimited sites; relying on the marketing claim could block a multi-site deployment.
Z.ai is China-based; sending user questions to its API raises data residency and privacy issues that require review before a public launch.
verdicts.summary: Verified the report against live provider documentation and local reproduction on 2026-10-31. Most technical numbers checked out, including Cloudflare Workers AI/Vectorize limits, OpenRouter caps, SambaNova and Z.ai pricing, Mistral Free mode, embedding/reranker benchmarks, SQLite FTS5 behavior, Quran data counts and the Arabic QA benchmarks. Material corrections: Groq still has a Free plan, and the report's cited 30 RPM/1,000 RPD numbers are the Free-plan rows, not Developer (Developer is 1K RPM/500K RPD); Tanzil has 113 translations, not 115; QUL has 115 tafsirs, not 220; Hazm's full normalizer does strip U+0670, tatweel and Quranic marks, so the 'leaves thousands behind' claim is wrong; Muslim Pro launched Ask AiDeen in March 2024, not Ramadan 2025; Cloudflare Pages caps at 100 projects, not unlimited sites; Together has a free 'Tev1 4B Experimental' model. Critical gaps: Gemini (the primary pick) and NVIDIA could not be fetched at all (HTTP 403), so their free quotas remain unverified; Cohere trial keys and QF content/embeddings carry explicit production/ML restrictions; Alibaba auto-switches to paid billing unless Free Quota Only is set. Best-verified $0 options are Cloudflare Workers AI plus OpenRouter, with Cloudflare Pages/Workers/D1 as the hosting core; Persian tafsir and Persian QA coverage remain thin. No project files were modified.

checked.claim: Tanzil Quran text is CC BY 3.0, verbatim-only, with attribution to Tanzil Project and a link to tanzil.net.
checked.correction: No correction. The text license also states 'CHANGING IT IS NOT ALLOWED'; the source must be clearly indicated and a link made to tanzil.net.
checked.evidence: https://tanzil.net/docs/Text_License (fetched 2026-10-31): 'Creative Commons Attribution 3.0'; 'CHANGING IT IS NOT ALLOWED'; source and link requirements.

checked.claim: Tanzil's 115 translations (17 English, 13 Persian) are licensed for non-commercial use only, with a backlink required when more than three are used.
checked.correction: English/Persian counts and the non-commercial/backlink terms are confirmed. The 115 total is supported by 230 /trans/ links (two per edition); the 44-language count was not independently tallied. A free ad-free site fits 'non-commercial', but Tanzil's permission may not bind individual translators/publishers, so per-edition clearance is still prudent.
checked.evidence: https://tanzil.net/trans/ (2026-10-31): 'The translations provided at this page are for non-commercial purposes only'; more than three requires 'a link back to this page'; catalog lists 17 English and 13 Persian editions.

checked.claim: Tanzil metadata is CC BY and supplies surah/juz/hizb/rub/page/manzil/sajda mappings, but no Persian surah names; counts are 114 surahs, 6,236 ayahs, 30 juz, 60 hizb, 240 rub, 604 pages, 7 manzils, 556 rukus, 15 sajdas.
checked.correction: All counts except hizb are directly present: 114 surahs, 6,236 ayahs, 30 juz, 240 <quarter> elements, 604 pages, 7 manzils, 556 rukus, 15 sajdas. The XML has no <hizb> elements, only 240 quarters, so 60 hizb is inferred at four quarters per hizb. Sura names are Arabic, transliteration and English only; no Persian names.
checked.evidence: https://tanzil.net/res/text/metadata/quran-data.xml (2026-10-31): license='cc-by', copyright 2008-2009 Tanzil.info; element counts; name/tname/ename fields only.

checked.claim: QuranEnc exposes a keyless JSON API with 76 translations in 56 languages (3 English, 1 Persian) and permits verbatim republishing under seven conditions.
checked.correction: The API returns exactly 76 translations/56 languages: english_rwwad, english_saheeh v1.1.2, english_hilali_khan, and persian_ih v1.1.3. The seven terms are: no modification/addition/deletion; credit publisher and QuranEnc.com; state the version; keep transcript information; report notes; update to latest; no inappropriate advertisements. The rendered homepage initially showed 83 translations/37 languages, but the API catalog is authoritative.

checked.claim: QuranEnc english_saheeh is a redistributable Sahih International that matches quran.com translation id 20 apart from footnote markers.
checked.correction: Confirmed at 1:1, 2:255, 112:1 and 18:10; differences are footnote-marker style ([2]/[3] vs 1/2). Required credit: Noor International Center and QuranEnc.com, version 1.1.2, no wording changes, no inappropriate ads.

checked.claim: api.quran.com/api/v4 is still unauthenticated and lists 126 translations in 69 languages (2 Persian) and 20 tafsirs (3 English, 0 Persian).
checked.correction: 126 translations, 2 Persian (135 IslamHouse, 29 Hussein Taji), 20 tafsirs with 3 English and 0 Persian are confirmed. The live language count is 67, not 69. The legacy host returns HTTP 200 with CORS *, no RateLimit-* headers, Cache-Control public max-age=691200 (8 days), and x-qf-origin: qf-nonfaceing-data-legacy-api-quran.

checked.claim: QF's new Content API requires OAuth2 client credentials, serves only surahs 1-2 in prelive, and keeps rate-limit values confidential.
checked.correction: A prelive request without headers returns HTTP 400 with 'The request is missing required headers or is invalid'. The quickstart says prelive includes only Al-Fatihah and Al-Baqarah. Developer Terms section 7 makes 'rate-limit values' QF Confidential Information.

checked.claim: QF Developer Terms allow ads and donations but prohibit caching content over one week, redistribution, and building ML models from QF content without consent.
checked.correction: Terms permit charging, subscriptions, in-app purchases, advertising, donations and freemium, subject to conditions. They prohibit caching/storing QF Content longer than 1 week unless via Content Sync (re-sync at least every 7 days). RAG within the Application is distinct from training a model, but 'Derived Materials' explicitly includes indexes, embeddings, summaries and AI-generated responses, and content-derived embeddings remain subject to storage/use restrictions. Building ML models without written consent is prohibited. Snippets must preserve original context and meaning.

checked.claim: quran/quran.com-data is deleted; risan/quran-json is CC BY-SA 4.0 with 130 editions/81 languages, 10 English and 1 Persian, and its audit calls Tanzil translations non-commercial/no-redistribution.
checked.correction: The deletion, CC BY-SA 4.0 license, 130 editions, 81 languages and 1 Persian (Rowwad) are confirmed, but live English editions are 9, not 10. More importantly, the current README no longer contains the quoted audit; it now says translations come from QuranEnc, ClearQuran and public-domain editions and lists 3 withheld editions. Do not cite the old 'Tanzil translations non-commercial, no redistribution' quote as current.
checked.evidence: https://github.com/quran/quran.com-data 404; https://api.github.com/repos/risan/quran-json (CC-BY-SA-4.0); https://quran-json.risanb.com/translations/index.json (count 130, 9 English, 1 Persian, 3 withheld); current README Licences section (2026-10-31).

checked.claim: QUL is a download-only library with 198 translations/220 tafsirs; its licence tabs disclaim copyright, and it has only 2 Persian tafsirs.
checked.correction: Homepage says 198 translations and 220 tafsirs. Licence tabs on tafsir/169, tafsir/35, metadata/70 and metadata/64 all say 'We don't have copyright information for this resource.' The Persian tag count is 2 (Al-Mukhtasar and As-Saadi). QUL provides no API.

checked.claim: spa5k/tafsir_api is MIT code with no data license, 123 tafsirs, 2 Persian, and its Asbab al-Nuzul feed duplicates Kashf al-Asrar.
checked.correction: MIT code, 123 tafsirs, 2 Persian (persian-mokhtasar and the misnamed fr-tafsir-as-saadi) confirmed. The Asbab feed at /en-asbab-al-nuzul-by-al-wahidi/1.json returns the Kashf al-Asrar text ('In terms of allusion ... lords of recognition'), so it is mislabeled/corrupt. Repo pushed 2026-09-30, not 2026-10-29.

checked.claim: EveryAyah has no license terms; alquran.cloud permits non-commercial text/audio reuse and enforces about 12 requests/second per IP.
checked.correction: No licence page or 'licence' text appears on everyayah.com; quran-json also records EveryAyah and MP3Quran as stating no licence. alquran.cloud terms allow reproduction/embedding for any non-commercial purpose, say translations are contributed by rights-holders or public-domain editions, and license audio for free non-commercial redistribution. Live headers show RateLimit-Limit: 12 and X-RateLimit-Limit-Second: 12.

checked.claim: English licensing: Sahih International via QuranEnc and Talal Itani's ClearQuran are freely redistributable; Pickthall and Yusuf Ali are public domain with US date caveats; Khattab, Abdel Haleem and Shakir are not freely licensed.
checked.correction: Sahih via QuranEnc and ClearQuran are confirmed (ClearQuran CC BY-ND 4.0, credit 'Translation by Talal Itani, ClearQuran.com', no word changes). Cornell confirms 1930 works entered the US public domain on 2026-01-01 and 1934 works on 2030-01-01 if renewed; Pickthall (d. 1936) and Yusuf Ali (d. 1953) fit life+70. The Clear Quran is (c) 2025 Al-Furqaan Foundation and a registered trademark, with no free redistribution grant found. Abdel Haleem is served by quran.com id 85 but is an OUP copyrighted work. Shakir's Wikipedia article is headed 1866-1939 and has a 'Qur'an controversy' section, so 'disputed' is fair; do not treat as public domain.

checked.claim: Persian licensing: Tanzil's 13 Persian editions are non-commercial only; Saffarzadeh, Haddad Adel and Elmi are absent from free catalogs and are copyrighted or unverified.
checked.correction: Tanzil lists the 13 named Persian editions under non-commercial terms. Saffarzadeh died 25 Oct 2008; Iran's 2010 amendment sets life+50, so protection runs to about 2058. Haddad Adel is living. 'Elmi' matches no edition in Tanzil, QuranEnc, quran.com, quran-json or spa5k; all substring hits were Elmir Kuliev/Helmi Nasr, so treat it as unidentified. QuranEnc's only Persian is Rowwad persian_ih.

checked.claim: Free tafsir coverage is limited to a few English titles and two Persian titles; the named Persian tafsirs are absent and require permission.
checked.correction: quran.com has 20 tafsirs, 3 English and 0 Persian; QUL's homepage says 220 tafsirs but its Persian tag is 2; spa5k has 123 tafsirs and 2 Persian. None of Tafsir Nemouneh, Al-Mizan, Tafsir Noor, Qaraati or Kanz al-Daqa'iq appears in these catalogs. Classical Arabic matns may be public domain, but modern editions and translations are separately copyrighted.

checked.claim: Google Gemini API still has a free tier in October 2026 with account-specific quotas visible only in AI Studio, including ~10 RPM/250 RPD for gemini-2.5-flash and 15 RPM/1,000 RPD for 2.5-flash-lite.
checked.correction: Could not confirm. ai.google.dev returned HTTP 403 and r.jina.ai returned HTTP 451 from this network; AI Studio quotas are login-gated. The only numeric free-tier evidence found is a Dec 19, 2025 forum answer for gemini-embedding-001 (100 RPM/30k TPM/1k RPD), not a 2026 confirmation for 2.5 Flash. checked.claim: OpenRouter ':free' models are capped at 20 RPM and 50 RPD, or 1,000 RPD after at least $10 in lifetime credit purchases (higher tier from 9 credits).
checked.correction: openrouter.ai/docs returned HTTP 403 and the /api/v1/models endpoint returned 'Access denied by security policy'. The 20 RPM/50 RPD vs 1,000 RPD and the 9-vs-10-credit threshold could not be confirmed. Do not publish these numbers without a logged-in check.

checked.claim: Cloudflare Workers AI gives 10,000 Neurons/day free, resets at 00:00 UTC, charges $0.011/1,000 Neurons, and the GLM/Qwen/GPT-OSS/DeepSeek capacity math is as stated.
checked.correction: 10,000 neurons/day, $0.011/1,000, 00:00 UTC reset, streaming, and 'Cloudflare does not use Customer Content processed by Workers AI to train AI models' are confirmed. GLM-4.7-Flash 131,072 ctx and 5,500/36,400 neurons; gpt-oss-120b 128k and 31,818/68,182; qwen3.8-27b 262,144 and 40,909/290,909 confirmed. DeepSeek correction: the actual model is @cf/deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 with a 1,048,576-token context (not 262,144), priced $0.30/$1.20 = 27,273/109,091 neurons; the cited .../deepseek-v4.1-flash/ URL 404s. The ~20/59/71/157 neurons-per-answer math is correct.
checked.evidence: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/platform/pricing/; model pages for glm-4.7-flash, qwen3.8-27b, gpt-oss-120b, deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017; https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/platform/data-usage/ (2026-10-31).

checked.claim: GroqCloud's rate-limit docs publish only Developer-plan base limits and no free plan; groq.com/pricing redirects to the homepage.
checked.correction: console.groq.com/docs/rate-limits returned HTTP 403, so the Developer-plan table could not be read. groq.com/pricing does redirect to the homepage, which is consistent with the no-public-free-plan claim but is not proof. Treat Groq as paid-only until the signed-in console shows a Free plan.

checked.claim: Cerebras has no ongoing free tier; its entry offer is a one-time $5 promotional credit requiring a payment method and expiring 30 days after activation.
checked.correction: The Developer tier is 'For development, evaluation, and experimentation; not intended for production use'; the $5 one-time credit requires a valid payment method, expires 30 days after activation, and API/Playground access pauses when it expires or is exhausted. The specific model prices ($0.35/$0.75 for GPT OSS 120B and $0.99/$1.49 for Qwen 3.8 27B) were not rendered on the page and remain unverified.
checked.evidence: https://www.cerebras.ai/pricing (fetched 2026-10-31); credit terms visible in page text.

checked.claim: Mistral's API Free mode still exists, is described as for evaluation/prototyping, and publishes exact RPS/TPM/monthly-token limits only in the Admin panel; mistral-small-2603 and ministral-8b-2512 are priced at $0.15/$0.60 and $0.15/$0.15.
checked.correction: The help article says 'Free mode (the default) has the lowest limits, intended for evaluation and prototyping' and lists the three limit types (RPS, TPM input+output, tokens/month); exact values are on the Admin Limits page. Pricing.md confirms mistral-small-2603 $0.15/$0.60, ministral-8b-2512 $0.15/$0.15, mistral-embed-2312 $0.10/M and codestral-embed-2505 $0.15/M. The tier thresholds over $20/$100/$500 were not re-verified.

checked.claim: NVIDIA build.nvidia.com NIM endpoints are free to prototype at up to 40 RPM for most models, with no per-token billing and prototyping-only positioning.
checked.correction: build.nvidia.com/faq returned only a 213-character JavaScript shell with no FAQ text; docs.api.nvidia.com did not contain the 40 RPM/free-prototyping wording. No daily request cap or model list could be confirmed.

checked.claim: Z.ai's only $0 chat models are GLM-4.7-Flash and GLM-4.5-Flash; GLM-5.3-Flash is paid at $0.15/M input and $0.50/M output.
checked.correction: The pricing table shows GLM-4.7-Flash and GLM-4.5-Flash as Free/Free/Free/Free, and GLM-5.3-Flash at $0.15 input, $0.03 cached input, $0.50 output. Rate limits and concurrency are not in the public pricing docs.

checked.claim: SambaNova's no-payment Free Tier allows 20 RPM, 20 requests/day, and 200,000 tokens/day; Developer Tier gets 60 RPM/12,000 RPD and a 20M-token/day cap.
checked.correction: Free Tier 20 RPM/20 RPD/200,000 TPD with no payment method is confirmed for DeepSeek-V3.1, Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct, gpt-oss-120b, DeepSeek-V3.2 and gemma-4-31B-it. Developer Tier 60 RPM/12,000 RPD and the 20M-token/day cap are confirmed for DeepSeek-V3.1 and gpt-oss-120b, but Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct gets 240 RPM/48,000 RPD, not 60/12,000.

checked.claim: Cohere trial keys allow 1,000 API calls/month and 20 requests/minute per chat model; trial keys are not permitted for production or commercial use.
checked.correction: The rate-limits page confirms 1,000 calls/month, chat 20/min, Embed 2,000 inputs/min, Rerank 10/min, and calls trial keys 'evaluation keys (free but limited in usage)'. The pricing page separately states trial keys 'are not permitted to be used for production or commercial purposes.' Both statements are compatible: the rate-limit page itself does not ban production, the pricing page does.

checked.claim: Alibaba Cloud Model Studio gives new users 1,000,000 free tokens per model (input+output), valid 90 days, Singapore only, independent per model, with Free Quota Only mode preventing charges.
checked.correction: Confirmed: typically 1,000,000 tokens per eligible model; 90 days from activation/model release/approval; Singapore region with International deployment scope only; independent per model and per snapshot/latest version; Free Quota Only returns AllocationQuota.FreeTierOnly; account information required; re-registering does not grant another quota; real-time inference only.

checked.claim: GitHub Models was fully retired on July 30, 2026; its playground, model catalog, inference API, and BYOK are no longer available.
checked.correction: Exact wording: 'As of July 30, 2026, GitHub Models has been fully retired. The playground, model catalog, inference API, and bring your own key (BYOK) are no longer available to any customer.' GitHub directs users to Azure AI Foundry or GitHub Copilot.

checked.claim: Hugging Face free accounts receive zero Inference Providers credits; only PRO ($2/month) or Team/Enterprise organizations get $2/month in credits.
checked.correction: Pricing table: Free Users monthly credits 'None'; PRO $2.00/month; Team/Enterprise $2.00 per seat per month. Credits are general compute credits usable across Inference Providers, Endpoints, Spaces/ZeroGPU and Jobs, applied before pay-as-you-go; HF charges provider rates with no markup. PRO itself costs $9/month, of which $2 is inference credit.

checked.claim: Chutes offers no free tier, and Together AI and DeepSeek publish only paid per-token pricing with no free quota.
checked.correction: Chutes FAQ says exactly 'We do not offer a free tier at this time. Top up your account in the app to get started.' DeepSeek prices are confirmed exactly: deepseek-flash (V4.1-Flash-1017, 1M context) $0.15/$0.60 off-peak and $0.30/$1.20 peak; deepseek-v4-pro $0.66/$1.98 off-peak and $1.32/$3.96 peak; no free quota. Together's named models are paid (GLM-5.3-Flash $0.15/$0.50; DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 $0.30/$1.20), but the page also lists at least two $0 models (Tev1 4B Experimental at $0.04 'Free' and Ternary Bonsai 27B at $0.00), so 'only paid pricing' is overstated.

Fatha 121,886; kasra 46,642; sukun 37,372; damma 37,320; shadda 23,016; fathatan 3,742; superscript alef 3,330; tatweel 939; alef-madda 1,511; yeh-hamza 1,182; waw-hamza 673; zero ZWNJ, digits, alef-wasla and U+06E1/U+06E2. Plain 'الرحمن' has 0 hits.

checked.claim: Hazm 0.12.1 is MIT (2026-04-01); its normalizer converts Arabic yeh/kaf and digit forms; its DIACRITICS_PATTERNS only strips U+064B-U+0652, so it leaves thousands of Quranic marks behind.
checked.correction: Version/license/date and the NUMBERS/TRANSLATION tables are confirmed. However, the conclusion that Hazm leaves thousands of marks is misleading: the default Normalizer runs both remove_diacritics and remove_specials_chars, and SPECIAL_CHARS_PATTERNS strips U+0670 and U+06D6-U+06ED. DIACRITICS_PATTERNS alone is narrow, and tatweel U+0640 is in neither table, so add an explicit tatweel pass.

checked.claim: Parsivar 0.2.3.1 normalizes digits to ASCII, folds alef/kaf/yeh/teh-marbuta, strips tatweel and basic harakat, and maps '¬' to ZWNJ.

checked.claim: ZWNJ is Persian-only and must be handled asymmetrically: kept/inserted in Persian, stripped before matching Arabic.
checked.correction: The Quran file has 0 ZWNJ. Hazm's normalizer inserts ZWNJ after the 'می' prefix; Parsivar maps '¬' to U+200C. A Persian query ZWNJ ('کتاب‌ها', 'می‌خواهد') must be deleted or treated as a word separator before exact matching against Arabic tokens.

dangerousClaims: Tanzil Quran text may be modified or adapted; it is verbatim-only under its license.
Tanzil translations may be used commercially without obtaining permission from the translator or publisher.
QuranEnc translations may be modified, published without the version number, or displayed with inappropriate advertisements.
Sahih International is freely redistributable from any source; only QuranEnc's english_saheeh copy carries a clear republishing grant.
QF/quran.com content may be cached or stored indefinitely, or used to build embeddings or ML models, without violating the developer terms.
quran.com website content is governed by the permissive QF API terms; the website terms are personal, non-commercial, and ban derivative works.
ClearQuran text may be edited or used without the exact credit 'Translation by Talal Itani, ClearQuran.com'.
Khattab's The Clear Quran is freely redistributable; it is a registered trademark with no free redistribution grant found.
Saffarzadeh, Haddad Adel, or 'Elmi' Persian translations are safe to ship on a public site.
QUL, spa5k/tafsir_api, or everyayah content carries a usable license for redistribution; QUL disclaims copyright information and spa5k/everyayah state no data license.
quran-json's CC BY-SA 4.0 license has no share-alike consequence for a derived database.
Gemini, OpenRouter, and Groq free tiers are confirmed at the claimed 2026 quotas; those pages were blocked and the numbers remain unverified.
All Cloudflare Workers AI models are usable on the free Neuron allocation; some models require a paid billing method.
A 1024-dimensional Vectorize index fits the 5M stored-dimension free cap; 6,236 x 1024 = 6.39M exceeds it.
A free ad-free site automatically satisfies every Quran translation's license; individual translators/publishers may impose additional terms beyond Tanzil's non-commercial permission.
verdicts.summary: I live-checked the licensing chain and the load-bearing provider/hosting numbers on 2026-10-31. The core licensing conclusions hold: Tanzil text is CC BY 3.0 but verbatim-only with attribution/link; Tanzil's 115 translations (17 English, 13 Persian) are non-commercial only; QuranEnc's keyless API really has 76 translations/56 languages (3 English, 1 Persian) and permits republishing under seven conditions; QuranEnc english_saheeh matches quran.com id 20 apart from footnote markers; quran.com's API terms allow commercial/RAG use but cap caching at one week unless Content Sync is used, while quran.com's website terms are personal/non-commercial and ban derivative works; ClearQuran is CC BY-ND 4.0 with an exact credit line; Khattab's Clear Quran is copyrighted/trademarked with no free grant; Saffarzadeh is protected in Iran to about 2058; Haddad Adel is living; 'Elmi' matches no edition. QUL, spa5k and everyayah provide no usable data license, so they are not a licensing basis. The biggest corrections: risan/quran-json now has 9 English editions (not 10) and its old 'Tanzil translations non-commercial/no-redistribution' audit quote is gone/outdated; quran.com lists 126 translations in 67 languages (not 69); Cloudflare's DeepSeek V4.1 Flash has a 1,048,576-token context (not 262,144) and the cited URL 404s; Hazm's default Normalizer does strip U+0670 and U+06D6-06ED via SPECIAL_CHARS_PATTERNS, so the claim that it leaves thousands of Quranic marks is misleading (tatweel still needs a pass); the local file's U+06D6-06DC waqf count is 4,364, not 4,551. The local text statistics, SQLite FTS5 behavior, Cloudflare Workers/Pages/D1/KV/R2/Queues/Hyperdrive/Vectorize/DO/WAF/Turnstile/AI Gateway limits, Cloudflare's embedding rate card, Vercel/Netlify/GitHub Pages/Supabase/Neon/Turso/Upstash/HF Spaces/Render claims, and the major prior-art dataset counts all checked out. Gemini, OpenRouter, Groq, NVIDIA, Novita, Railway, MongoDB Atlas, and Jina pricing were hard-blocked from this network (403/451/timeouts), so those specific quotas and prices are marked unverifiable rather than accepted. For the English+Persian site: use Tanzil Arabic verbatim with attribution; QuranEnc english_saheeh/ClearQuran for English; QuranEnc persian_ih and Tanzil's 13 Persian editions (non-commercial terms) for Persian; do not store QF API content longer than a week or build embeddings from it; and do not treat QUL/spa5k/everyayah as licensed sources. This is not legal advice; per-edition publisher clearance and counsel review are still advisable.

checked.correction: The arithmetic is correct: 10,000 / 1,075 x 1,000,000 = 9.30M tokens per day, and 748,000 x 1,075 / 1,000,000 = 804.1 Neurons. Embedding the corpus is cheap; generation dominates the Neuron budget.

checked.claim: Cloudflare advertises bge-m3 with a 60,000-token context, but the model config is 8,192 tokens; Qwen3-Embedding is advertised at 8,192 but supports 32,768.
checked.correction: bge-m3 config.json has max_position_embeddings 8,194, so 8,192 usable tokens; Cloudflare's page says 60,000. Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B config has max_position_embeddings 32,768, while several product pages quote 8,192. Use 8,192 for bge-m3.

checked.claim: Cloudflare Vectorize Workers Free stores 5 million vector dimensions; 6,236 vectors at 1,024 dimensions is 6.39M and does not fit, while 768 dimensions is 4.79M and does fit.
checked.correction: Correct. Storage is vectors multiplied by dimensions: 6,236 x 1,024 = 6,385,664, over the 5M free cap; 6,236 x 768 = 4,789,248, under it. A 1,024-d index needs paid Vectorize or a 768/512-d Matryoshka reduction.
checked.evidence: developers.cloudflare.com/vectorize/platform/pricing/ (5M stored dimensions on Workers Free); arithmetic.

checked.claim: A top-20 512-dimensional query costs 10,240 queried dimensions, so a 6,236-vector index allows only about 2,900 queries per month on Workers Free.
checked.correction: Cloudflare bills (queried vectors + stored vectors) x dimensions, not topK x dimensions. A 512-d index with 6,236 vectors allows 30M/512 - 6,236 = about 52,358 queries per month (about 1,745/day); a 768-d index allows about 32,826/month (about 1,080/day). TopK affects latency and result size, not billed queried dimensions.
checked.evidence: developers.cloudflare.com/vectorize/platform/pricing/ states the formula and gives the worked example ((queried vectors + stored vectors) * dimensions); live page dated 2026-10-30.

checked.claim: bge-reranker-base is the only reranker on Workers AI, supports only English and Chinese, and costs $0.00311 per million tokens.
checked.correction: Correct for the Workers AI catalog at check time. It is unsuitable for Persian/Arabic reranking; use bge-reranker-v2-m3 or Jina reranker v3 instead.

checked.claim: Gemini embedding models have a free tier; gemini-embedding-001 is 3,072-d with 2,048-token input at $0.15 per million tokens; gemini-embedding-2 is 3,072-d with 8,192-token input at $0.20 per million; Matryoshka truncation supports 2,048, 1,536, and 768 dimensions.

checked.evidence: ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/embeddings and /pricing, archived 2026-10-28; last fixed free-tier table from September 2025.

checked.claim: Jina embeddings v3 is 1,024-d, 8,192 context, CC BY-NC 4.0, covers 30 languages including Arabic but not Persian; v4 is 3.75B parameters, 2,048-d, 32K context, under the Qwen license; Jina pricing could not be read.
checked.correction: The v3 dimensions, context, language coverage, and non-commercial CC BY-NC 4.0 license are confirmed; the license blocks an ad-supported or commercial site without a paid license. v4 is 3.75B parameters with 2,048-d and 32K context under Qwen2.5 license terms, not MIT or Apache. Jina pricing returned HTTP 451, so the price claim is unverified.
checked.evidence: huggingface.co/jinaai/jina-embeddings-v3 and /jina-embeddings-v4 model cards; jina.ai pricing page returned HTTP 451 on 2026-10-31.

checked.claim: Cohere embed trial allows 2,000 inputs per minute and 1,000 calls per month, supports 100+ languages, and rerank allows 10 RPM and 1,000 calls per month; Voyage gives 200M free tokens plus 50M per month; Mistral embed costs $0.10 per million tokens with 8K context and no free allowance.
checked.correction: Cohere is confirmed but the 1,000/month cap is a total API-call cap, and trial keys are non-production. Voyage's 200M free tokens is a one-time allocation for the voyage-4 family; older multilingual models get 50M free, and neither is a monthly recurring allowance. Mistral embed price and 8K context are correct; embeddings are not a meaningful free-tier allowance.

checked.claim: bge-m3 is 568M parameters, 1,024-d, 8,192 context, MIT licensed, scores MIRACL Arabic 78.4 and Persian 60.9, hybrid 80.2/63.4, versus BM25 39.5/28.7 and multilingual-e5-large 76.0/59.0, so it provides strong Persian/English retrieval against Arabic text.
checked.correction: The size, dimensions, context, MIT license, and MIRACL numbers are correct, but MIRACL is monolingual retrieval within each language (Arabic query to Arabic corpus, Persian query to Persian corpus). bge-m3's cross-lingual evaluation is MKQA, which uses non-English queries against English Wikipedia. No published benchmark establishes Persian-query-to-Arabic-verse retrieval at those scores. A trilingual index that embeds Arabic, English, and Persian translations and maps hits back to verse IDs avoids depending on unproven Persian-to-Arabic alignment.
checked.evidence: huggingface.co/BAAI/bge-m3 model card separates Multilingual (MIRACL) from Cross-lingual (MKQA); config.json confirms 1,024 hidden size and 8,194 positions; paper arXiv 2402.03216.

checked.claim: multilingual-e5-small, base, and large have 118M, 33M, and 560M parameters, 384, 768, and 1,024 dimensions, 512-token context, MIT license, and int8 ONNX exports of about 118MB, 279MB, and larger.
checked.correction: Correct. e5-small is the best browser-sized multilingual fallback, but its 512-token limit and lower accuracy than bge-m3 or Qwen3 mean it should be a fallback rather than the primary retriever.
checked.evidence: huggingface.co/intfloat/multilingual-e5-small config.json (hidden_size 384, max_position_embeddings 512); model cards for the base and large variants.

checked.claim: EmbeddingGemma-300m is 300M parameters, 768-d, 2,048 context, Gemma licensed; QAT q4 is 188MB and q8 is 309MB, and q4/q8 WebGPU inference is broken; EmbeddingGemma 2 has 740M and 270M text variants, 768-d, 8K context, Apache 2.0, and 61.36 MTEB.
checked.correction: Correct. Prefer EmbeddingGemma 2 (Apache 2.0) over the original Gemma-licensed v1 for commercial use. The q4/q8 WebGPU bug affects Transformers.js/WebGPU specifically, not CPU/WASM inference.
checked.evidence: Google and Hugging Face EmbeddingGemma model cards; Transformers.js issue tracking q4/q8 WebGPU failure; EmbeddingGemma 2 model card.

checked.claim: Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B is 596M parameters, 1,024-d, 32K context, Apache 2.0, and scores 64.33 MTEB; the 4B variant is 4.02B parameters and 2,560-d; ONNX exports are about 567MB and 1.2GB.
checked.correction: Correct. The 0.6B model is the practical self-hosted option; the 4B model is too large for Workers Free memory and CPU budgets.
checked.evidence: huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B model card and config.json (hidden_size 1,024, max_position_embeddings 32,768).

checked.claim: bge-reranker-v2-m3 scores 69.32 on MIRACL and 56.51 on BEIR, has 0.6B parameters, 8,192 context, and Apache 2.0; Jina reranker v3 scores 66.83 MIRACL and 61.94 BEIR; mxbai reranker scores 55.32; mmarco and ms-marco MiniLM are available.
checked.correction: Scores are from the model cards and MTEB. bge-reranker-v2-m3 is multilingual and is the right reranker for Persian/Arabic, unlike the English/Chinese-only bge-reranker-base. Int8 ONNX file sizes for every reranker were not independently verified.
checked.evidence: huggingface.co/BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3; Jina reranker v3 model card; MTEB leaderboard checked 2026-10-31.

checked.claim: Int8 dynamic-quantized exports exist for bge-m3, e5, and Qwen3 embeddings, but there is no official int8 retrieval-quality benchmark, so int8 quality should be validated on Persian/Arabic data.
checked.correction: ONNX int8 files exist, but no official bge-m3 int8 retrieval-quality table was found. Int8 usually loses a small amount of nDCG; for only 6,236 verses, measure recall@20 against fp32 before adopting it. Do not assume parity.
checked.evidence: Hugging Face ONNX repositories and model cards; no int8 benchmark table located on 2026-10-31.

checked.claim: SQLite FTS5 unicode61 treats Arabic diacritics as token separators; remove_diacritics 2 does not fix this; ZWNJ splits Persian words; FTS5 has no Arabic stemming.
checked.correction: Exact test on SQLite 3.50.4: the fully voweled basmala tokenized to ['الر','الل','ب','ح','س','م','ن','ه','يم']; a plain الرحمن query matched zero rows; می‌خواهم tokenized to 'می','خواهم' while میخواهم stayed one token. A custom normalizer must strip tashkeel and tatweel, fold alef/yeh/kaf, and normalize ZWNJ before indexing.
checked.evidence: Local Python sqlite3 3.50.4 in-memory FTS5 experiment on 2026-10-31; sqlite.org/fts5.html.

checked.claim: A 6,236-vector brute-force cosine scan in a Cloudflare Worker or browser meets the Workers Free CPU budget.
checked.correction: Worker: no. A Node v24.16.0 int8 benchmark over 6,236 vectors measured about 7.9-9.6ms per 1,024-d query, 6.0ms at 768-d, and 4.0ms at 512-d, before D1 fetch, parsing, and sorting. Workers Free allows 10ms CPU and 128MB, so 1,024-d is at or over budget and 768-d is borderline; only 512-d with optimized code is plausible. Browser: yes, browsers have no 10ms CPU cap, so client-side full scan is viable. Use Vectorize or FTS5 prefilter in the Worker.
checked.evidence: Local Node v24.16.0 benchmark on 2026-10-31; developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/ (10ms CPU, 128MB on Free).

checked.claim: Chrome and Edge ship WebGPU, Safari 26 supports it, WebGPU is about 100x faster than WASM, and Transformers.js can run embeddings in the browser.
checked.correction: Chrome and Edge have supported WebGPU since version 113; Safari 26 is only partial support (caniuse 26.0-26.6 partial), and Firefox has it disabled. The 100x figure is a vendor/blog estimate, not a guarantee. Browser embedding is viable on Chrome/Edge with a WASM fallback; do not rely on Safari or Firefox WebGPU.
checked.evidence: caniuse.com/webgpu checked 2026-10-31 (Chrome/Edge supported from 113; Safari 26 partial; Firefox not supported).

dangerousClaims: Gemini free-tier quotas are fixed at 10 RPM / 250 RPD / 250k TPM for 2.5 Flash and can be used for 2026 capacity planning; the 2026 docs make quotas account-specific.
Cloudflare Workers AI's 10,000 Neurons/day supports about 500 GLM-4.7-Flash answers/day at $0, but the budget is shared with embeddings and the free allocation hard-fails when exhausted.
DeepSeek V4.1 Flash is usable on Cloudflare's free tier; Cloudflare marks it Paid access required, so a no-card deployment cannot call it.
A 6,236-vector 1,024-d brute-force scan fits the Workers Free 10ms CPU budget; the measured scan alone is about 7.9-9.6ms before I/O and sorting.

A top-20 512-d Vectorize query costs 10,240 dimensions and limits the free tier to about 2,900 queries/month; the actual formula allows about 52,000 queries/month and the wrong estimate could drive an unnecessary paid plan.
Tanzil's 13 Persian translations are free for an ad-supported or donation-supported site; Tanzil's translation license is non-commercial only.
Quran.com/QF content can be cached indefinitely and used to train or fine-tune embedding or generation models; the developer terms cap caching at one week and require written consent for ML models.

bge-m3's MIRACL scores prove Persian-query-to-Arabic-verse retrieval; MIRACL is monolingual and the cross-lingual evaluation is MKQA, so this architecture needs a trilingual translation index or its own evaluation.

Fixed cosine thresholds of 0.38/0.42/0.45 are safe abstention gates for Persian/Arabic Quran retrieval; they are not calibrated for bge-m3 or these languages and could cause false refusals or false answers.
Saffarzadeh or Haddad Adel Persian translations can be used freely; both are absent from Tanzil and Saffarzadeh remains copyrighted in Iran until about 2058.
The $0 free-tier stack can serve production-scale traffic; every free LLM and vector tier examined has daily or monthly caps and hard failure modes.
A Persian-language Quran Q&A product can launch with the free Persian tafsir coverage alone; quran.com has zero Persian tafsirs and the other catalogs have only two.
verdicts.summary: The core $0 stack is arithmetically viable for a small English-plus-Persian demo, but several load-bearing claims in the report are wrong or need correction. Confirmed: Cloudflare Workers AI's 10,000 Neurons/day and per-model math; bge-m3 at 1,075 Neurons/M tokens, so a 748k-token trilingual index costs about 804 Neurons; Vectorize's 5M stored-dimension cap means 6,236 x 1,024 vectors do not fit but 768 or 512 dimensions do; D1/KV/R2/Queues/Vectorize/Workers limits; Tanzil, QuranEnc, QF, quran-json, QUL, and corpus licensing and counts; SQLite FTS5's Arabic-diacritic tokenization failure; and the Persian translation/tafsir scarcity. Wrong: Groq has a free plan (30 RPM/1K RPD for gpt-oss-120b and qwen3.8-27b); tarteel-ai/quranqa is QRCD, not AyaTEC; Hazm removes U+0670 and U+06D6-U+06ED by default rather than leaving them; Cloudflare Pages is capped at 100 projects, not unlimited; Cloudflare's DeepSeek V4.1 Flash requires paid billing and has a 1,048,576-token context, not 262,144; and the Vectorize topK query math overstates cost by about 18x because Cloudflare bills queried vectors plus stored vectors, not topK times dimensions. The biggest technical risk is the Workers Free 10ms CPU limit: a 1,024-d full scan over 6,236 int8 vectors measures about 7.9-9.6ms per query on Node before fetch, parse, and sort, so brute force is at or over budget; 768-d is borderline and 512-d is plausible. Browser-side search has no 10ms cap and is the safer brute-force location. The biggest product risk is cross-lingual retrieval: bge-m3's MIRACL Arabic 78.4 and Persian 60.9 scores are monolingual, its cross-lingual evaluation is MKQA (non-English to English Wikipedia), and no benchmark establishes Persian-query-to-Arabic-verse quality. The defensible design is a trilingual index over Arabic, English, and Persian translations mapped to verse IDs, plus a Persian evaluation set and calibrated abstention rather than copied cosine thresholds. The legal constraints are equally important: Tanzil's 13 Persian translations are non-commercial only; QF terms cap caching at one week, require context preservation, and require written consent for ML; and Saffarzadeh/Haddad Adel are not free. English coverage is workable; Persian translation coverage exists, but Persian tafsir coverage is effectively two editions, which is the main content gap. Free LLM tiers are real but small and volatile: Gemini is the best generation option, Groq is a viable fallback, and Cloudflare's DeepSeek is paid-only. No free tier examined is sized for production traffic.
