scores.name: Faater Quran Q&A (فاطر)
scores.rationale: Only proposal whose $0 is structural: the request path is static files, so 100k and 10M queries cost the same and there is no card, server, key or query quota that can fail or bill. Displayed Arabic is byte-pinned to Tanzil and the renderer can emit only corpus strings, so fabricated verses, invented citations and fake tafsir are structurally impossible — the strongest answer to Dar al-Ifta-style content rules and the reason legal safety is 9.5. English and Persian are full peers: UI, refusal and boundary copy, 114 Persian surah names, RTL, Persian digits and Jalali dates. The price is conversational quality: BM25 plus a 300-concept lexicon gives limited paraphrase and Persian cross-lingual recall, no prose explanation, and the theta/coverage gates remain provisional until the 600-item calibration, hence answer quality 6 and refusal reliability 8.

scores.name: Tibyan (تبیان) — Quran Q&A
scores.rationale: Best data-integrity discipline in the set: an official Tanzil Simple Clean search copy with a 99.5% normalized-agreement check, analyzer versioning, a learned domain classifier and sufficiency gate, and hard citation/quote validation for opt-in BYOK generation. There is no operator key and no bill path, and lexical mode survives any external CDN failure. But the 118 MB int8 / 235 MB fp16 in-browser model is a product-level tax: most mobile users — especially in Iran, where Hugging Face may be blocked — will stay lexical-only, so real-world quality collapses toward the winner while build effort (8-12 weeks) and bandwidth rise sharply (about 2.6 TB/month at 100k cold loads, 10-25 TB at 1M). e5-small is materially weaker than bge-m3 on classical Arabic and Persian, and BYOK generation is opt-in with browser key-handling risk.

scores.name: Faater Quran Q&A (Faater-QA)
scores.rationale: Best retrieval and the only design that can produce grounded prose: bge-m3 trilingual views, D1 FTS5, RRF, percentile-calibrated gates and claim-level citation validation are well specified, and its Persian path is the strongest of the three. But the $0 claim is a traffic-model bet, not an architecture: 3,333 queries/day against a free LLM pool of roughly 1,000 answers/day, a 55% cache-hit assumption, Upstash's 10k ops/day ceiling, and an admitted paid overflow ($16-$250/month depending on volume) mean it is not a free public service at the target. Ten free providers multiply terms-change risk, LLM synthesis reintroduces interpretive error and privacy exposure (Gemini training, Z.ai China residency), and 17-20 person-weeks plus 0.25 FTE ops is heavy for a volunteer project.

judgement.bestPartsOfEach:
From Tibyan (second place, 43/60):
1) Independent search-copy cross-check — adopt Tanzil's official quran-simple-clean.txt as a second artifact and assert normalized agreement with the normalized display text at >=99.5%, logging every mismatch. Use it as a build diagnostic, not a hard gate, because Imlaei-vs-Simple-Clean orthography legitimately differs; the winner derives its index only from the display file and cannot independently detect normalization drift.
2) Learned retrieval-sufficiency gate — replace the winner's provisional theta and 0.34 coverage cutoffs with Tibyan's exported logistic model over top1 score, top1-top5 margin, BM25 z-score, content-term coverage, cross-field consensus, query length, domain probability and exact-reference flag, calibrated to <=2% false answers and <=10-12% false refusals; retain the deterministic gates as bootstrap fallbacks.
3) Compact domain classifier and intent routing — graft the hashed character 3-5 gram plus unigram logistic classifier (~300 KB int8, 3,000-5,000 synthetic/edited plus 500 gold EN/FA items) to replace the 80%-OOV off-topic heuristic, and route its five classes (quran_topic, fiqh, history, personal_guidance, off_topic) with fiqh boundary and reflection modes; require native Persian review of the gold set and keep an uncertain-retrieves band.
4) Persian normalization gold tests — adopt می‌خواهم، کتاب‌ها، الرحمن and ۲۵۵→255, plus the explicit bans on Hazm/Parsivar defaults for Quranic Arabic and the [ء-ي] filter for Persian; the winner tests corpus statistics but not these destructive regressions.
5) Analyzer and pack versioning — store the analyzer version in the index header and fail the build on mismatch; if an embedding pack is added, pin model revision, precision, dimension and SHA-256, and never mix an int8 index with an fp16 query model.
6) Result diversity — add Tibyan's MMR lambda=0.7 and max two verses per surah so the five cards are not near-duplicates from one passage; this is a zero-cost relevance gain.
7) Offline PWA — add a versioned service-worker pack with atomic cache swap; with the winner's 1-1.4 MB index, offline install is nearly free and removes the host from repeat use.
8) Edition coverage — add Talal Itani ClearQuran (CC BY-ND 4.0) as a second English edition and order editions with the user-language one first; the winner ships only one English translation.
9) Generation validator, only if prose is ever added — copy the JSON schema, candidate whitelist, exact quote-substring check, language check, no-repair discard rule and the exact 'AI draft could not be verified... discarded' notice; make it BYOK/local-only so the operator holds no key.

From Faater-QA (third place, 36.5/60):
1) Dense-first trilingual retrieval, not rerank-only — the winner's optional Phase 2 scans only FTS-prefiltered candidates, so it cannot recover a Persian paraphrase that shares no lexeme with the translation, the exact gap it is meant to close. Graft Faater-QA's three-views-per-verse index (Arabic Simple Clean, English Sahih, Persian Rowwad, bge-m3 1024-d) as a dense candidate generator fused with FTS by RRF, indexing at least the Persian translation view alongside Arabic. This is the highest-value losing idea.
2) Percentile calibration protocol — tau_dense = 5th percentile of answerable dev top-1 cosine, tau_rrf = 5th percentile of answerable RRF, tau_bm25 = 10th percentile of answerable BM25, tau_dense_hi where at most 5% of unanswerable queries exceed it; re-fit monthly and prohibit copied constants such as 0.38/0.42/0.45. Adopt for the winner's theta and coverage gates.
3) Stratified bilingual eval — 500-600 items with 25% unanswerable/off-topic, 15% fiqh-boundary and 10% sensitive, native Persian review, QRCD/IslamicFaithQA auxiliary only; the winner's 600-item set should adopt these quotas.
4) Scholar governance — 100 random answers/month plus every sensitive card reviewed pre-launch; the winner has only a lexicon reviewer, not an ongoing answer-review board.
5) Claim-level citation validator — every claim cites a retrieved verse, citations are a subset of retrieved ids, quoted spans are exact substrings, and ruling language outside quotes is rejected; one temperature-0 retry, then a deterministic card. Graft into any optional LLM tier.
6) Explicit degradation ladder — normal -> conservative -> cards_only with per-provider headroom and a circuit breaker at 90%, plus the invariant that any added component must hard-fail rather than bill; copy the state machine and user-facing status banner, not the ten-provider list.
7) Token budgeting — max 8 verses, truncate translations before Arabic, test each provider's tokenizer and reserve 300 output tokens; Arabic script inflates token counts and this is a concrete safeguard if prose is added.
8) Negative finding worth keeping — @cf/baai/bge-reranker-base is English/Chinese only and must not be used for Arabic or Persian; do not add a cross-encoder reranker without a multilingual model.
9) Cache design — exact plus semantic at cosine >=0.96, same language, entity check, versioned invalidation — only if a server tier is ever added; it is irrelevant to the static winner.
judgement.verdict: Winner: Faater Quran Q&A (فاطر), 52/60. It is the only proposal whose $0 claim is architectural rather than a traffic bet: static files, no server, no API key, no query quota and no path to a bill at 100k or 10M queries/month. It is also strongest on the two things the brief says to punish — free-tier fragility (its only dependency is commodity static hosting, with a second mirror) and religiously incorrect output (no model writes the answer; verses and citations come only from the byte-pinned corpus, so fabrication is structurally impossible). I verified the local corpus is 1,353,702 bytes, 6,266 lines and SHA-256 b3638f5cf03e2b05e4000efc0e4b656aafb3cf6ed28f8770b6497c5b43c46089, exactly as فاطر and Tibyan claim. Its price is real: BM25 plus a 300-concept lexicon gives limited paraphrase and Persian cross-lingual recall, no prose explanation, and provisional refusal thresholds, hence answer quality 6/10. Tibyan (43/60) is the correct runner-up; graft its independent Simple Clean cross-check, learned sufficiency and domain gates, Persian gold tests, analyzer versioning, MMR diversity and offline PWA. Its 118-235 MB in-browser model, not its safety design, is why it loses: most mobile and Iran-based users remain lexical-only while free-CDN bandwidth becomes the scaling bottleneck. Faater-QA (36.5/60) has the best retrieval and the only grounded prose, but its own numbers disqualify it as a free public service: about 1,000 free answers/day against 3,333/day demand, a 55% cache assumption, Upstash's 10k ops/day ceiling, admitted paid overflow, and residual LLM interpretive and privacy risk. The recommended build is فاطر v1, with Tibyan's calibrated gates and Faater-QA's dense trilingual candidate generator added only as a measured, hard-failing Phase 2 quality upgrade.

final.architecture:
Faater v1 is a static, client-side Quran answer engine for English and Persian. Its defining invariant is architectural, not policy-based: no model writes an answer. The renderer can emit only UI copy or byte-exact rows from the pinned corpus, so a fabricated verse, a wrong citation or invented tafsir is structurally impossible. The site is free, public, ad-free, donation-free and paid-tier-free, with no login, no cookies, no analytics and no server in the answer path. Questions never leave the device.

Scope is locked to English and Persian. Both are full peers: UI chrome, prompts, refusal and boundary copy, disclaimers, error states, the licenses page and all 114 surah names exist in both, and the build fails if any i18n key is missing. Arabic is always displayed as the source text but is not a third UI language. Adding a language later is a data-only pipeline run.

The design merges the judge's winner (فاطر, 52/60) with the best losing ideas. From فاطر it keeps the static host, byte-pinned Tanzil text, browser BM25, the 300-concept lexicon, the Verse Card contract, dual-host failover and exact refusal copy. From Tibyan it adds the learned domain classifier and retrieval-sufficiency model, the independent Tanzil Simple Clean cross-check, Persian normalization gold tests, analyzer versioning, MMR diversity, a second English edition and an offline PWA. From Faater-QA it adds percentile calibration, the stratified bilingual eval, scholar governance, the claim-level validator for any future prose tier, the explicit degradation ladder, token budgeting, the bge-reranker negative finding, and only as a measured Phase 2 the dense trilingual candidate generator. It rejects Faater-QA's ten-provider LLM cascade, semantic cache, Upstash/Vectorize dependency and paid overflow as part of the promise; it rejects Tibyan's 118-235 MB in-browser model as a default.

v1 is deliberately not conversational. It answers with ranked Verse Cards: Arabic verbatim, the user-language translation, plus or minus one verse of context, citation links and disclosure. That is the price of zero hallucination and zero cost. Quality is measured by Recall@10, refusal precision/recall and citation validity, not prose fluency. A prose mode is Phase 3 only, BYOK or separately funded, never on the $0 path.

DELIVERY
Cloudflare Pages Free is the primary host. It provides unlimited static requests and bandwidth subject to Cloudflare's terms, 100 projects per account, 500 builds per month, 20,000 files per deployment and 25 MiB per asset; about two builds per month are used. GitHub Pages is a byte-identical mirror with a 1 GB site cap and 100 GB/month soft bandwidth, so it is failover only, not primary at scale. There is no card on either host, no API key, no server, and no runtime third-party script. The only network requests are static assets. Artifacts are committed, hashed and immutable-cached; production never rebuilds.

CORPUS AND EDITIONS
Resources/quran-simple.txt is pinned and tracked. It is 1,353,702 bytes, 6,266 lines, 6,236 pipe-delimited verses, 114 surahs, with the 28-line Tanzil copyright block at lines 6239-6266, SHA-256 b3638f5cf03e2b05e4000efc0e4b656aafb3cf6ed28f8770b6497c5b43c46089. Despite the filename it is fully vowelled Tanzil Simple v1.1 text, not Tanzil Simple Clean: it contains 939 tatweel, 3,330 superscript alef and 0 ZWNJ. It is never edited. Display and index copies are separate files on separate code paths; a byte-equality test asserts the display artifact equals the pinned source. The index is derived from the display file with a documented normalizer, and Tanzil's official quran-simple-clean.txt is used only as an independent build-time cross-check: at least 99.5% normalized agreement, every mismatch logged, structural errors fail the build.

English defaults to QuranEnc english_saheeh v1.1.2 (Sahih International, Noor International Center) with the required credit and the seven republishing conditions reproduced on /licenses. Talal Itani ClearQuran (CC BY-ND 4.0, exact credit) is the second English edition, collapsed by default. Persian ships QuranEnc persian_ih v1.1.3 (Rowwad Translation Center) only, because it carries an explicit republishing grant. Tanzil Persian editions (Ghomshei, Makarem, Ansarian, Fooladvand) are not shipped until each edition's rights are cleared in writing; Tanzil's translation license is non-commercial only and individual translators or publishers may impose additional terms. No tafsir in v1: no free Persian tafsir with a usable license was found, and showing an English tafsir inside a Persian UI would misrepresent the product.

Metadata comes from Tanzil quran-data.xml (CC BY 3.0) for surah, juz, hizb, rub, page, sajda and English/Arabic names, plus a hand-authored 114-entry Persian surah-name table because no free catalog publishes Persian names. Sajda counts conflict across free sources (Tanzil 15, quran.com 14); v1 uses Tanzil 15 with a source note or omits sajda UI until resolved.

REPO LAYOUT
Resources/quran-simple.txt          pinned display text, tracked, SHA-256
data/meta.json                      versions, hashes, thresholds, editions
data/verses/001.json ... 114.json   display rows plus translations and context
data/index/{ar,en,fa}.qidx          QIDX1 BM25 field indexes
data/index/lite.qidx               1,200-verse Save-Data fallback
data/lexicon/concepts.json         300 concepts at launch, 500 target
data/gates/domain.bin              int8 logistic classifier
data/gates/sufficiency.json        weights and calibration metadata
data/licenses/*.txt                Tanzil, QuranEnc and ClearQuran texts
scripts/*.mjs                      build-time only
web/                               HTML, TypeScript, CSS, fonts, service worker
tests/                             golden queries, normalization, eval

REQUEST PATH
1. The app loads meta.json, then the active language pack: the language index plus the shared Arabic expansion index. SHA-256 is verified with SubtleCrypto before parsing. A mismatch shows the pre-rendered fallback, never a partial answer.
2. Input is trimmed, length-capped at 500 characters, stripped of bidi controls U+202A-U+202E and U+2066-U+2069, and script-detected. Queries are never rendered as HTML.
3. A verse-reference parser handles 2:255, 2.255, 2/255, Al-Baqarah 255, Surah 2 Ayah 255, سوره بقره آیه ۲۵۵, آیه ۲۵۵ بقره and Arabic-script equivalents. A valid reference resolves exactly and skips retrieval gates; an out-of-range reference returns a clarification with the valid range, never a guessed verse.
4. The learned domain classifier returns five classes: quran_topic, fiqh, history, personal_guidance, off_topic. Off-topic refuses before retrieval. Fiqh routes to the boundary card. Personal guidance routes to reflection cards. History allows Quranic verses only. The uncertain band retrieves and lets the sufficiency model decide.
5. The query is normalized with the exact build-time functions. Persian is a two-stage pass: ZWNJ handling, digit mapping and Persian yeh/kaf first, then the shared Arabic fold. Persian letters پ, چ, ژ, گ and ی survive every step.
6. Content terms expand through concepts.json into English, Persian and Arabic root or lemma sets. Unmapped terms pass through unchanged. This is the only cross-lingual bridge in v1.
7. BM25 runs over the loaded field indexes with k1=1.2 and b=0.75. Query-language field weight is 1.0; Arabic expansion weight is 0.85; the other-language expansion weight is 0.6 only when that pack is deliberately loaded.
8. Per-verse score is max(field score) plus 0.15 times min(2, number of fields with a hit). An exact phrase hit adds 0.2. A reference match overrides all scoring.
9. Ranked lists fuse with reciprocal rank fusion, k=60, top 40. MMR over normalized token sets (Jaccard similarity) with lambda=0.7 and a maximum of two verses per surah selects the final five cards, range three to eight.
10. The sufficiency model scores top-1, top-1/top-5 margin, BM25 z-score, content-term coverage, cross-field consensus, query length, domain probability and exact-reference flag. Below the calibrated per-language threshold, the response is refused_no_retrieval. The deterministic coverage and theta gates remain as bootstrap fallbacks only.
11. The Verse Card renders Arabic first, then the user-language translation, a collapsed second edition, one verse before and after, quran.com and tanzil.net links, the exact disclosure and a terms-I-searched-for panel. No generated commentary.

REFUSAL AND TRUST
Refusal is architectural first: the renderer cannot emit a verse that did not come from the corpus. It is gate-based second: input sanity, reference parsing, domain classification, sufficiency, fiqh boundary, sensitive-topic context and output contract. Every response carries not_a_fatwa, translation_not_quran, tafsir_shown:false and generated_commentary:false. Fiqh markers produce answered_with_boundary, never a ruling. Sensitive topics force the full verse, adjacent verses, at least two translations where available and a neutral context panel, with no editorial framing and no visible taxonomy label. The exact copy is in the refusal spec.

PRIVACY AND SECURITY
There is no server and no analytics, so questions never leave the device. This is a genuine architectural guarantee, stated plainly on the privacy page. CSP is default-src 'self'; no third-party scripts; no cookies; no localStorage of queries beyond the current session; share links carry only a verse reference and language, never the question.

OPTIONAL PHASE 2 DENSE PATH
Only if the eval shows a persistent recall gap after lexicon expansion. Cloudflare Worker Free plus D1 Free plus Workers AI @cf/baai/bge-m3. Precompute 18,708 int8 vectors, three views per verse (Arabic, English, Persian). Build 256 IVF clusters over the 6,236 verse centroids; bundle the 256 centroids in the Worker. At query time, embed once, compare to 256 centroids, shortlist 8 clusters, fetch about 570 view vectors from D1 as eight rows, and cosine-rerank. This is not FTS-prefiltered, so a Persian paraphrase with no shared lexeme can still reach the Arabic and English views. The Worker Free budget is 100,000 requests/day, 10 ms CPU and 128 MB; D1 Free is 5 GB, 5 million rows read/day and 100,000 rows written/day; Workers AI Free is 10,000 neurons/day and hard-fails at the cap. The candidate scan is roughly 850,000 int8 multiply-accumulates, estimated under 1 ms but required to be benchmarked under 10 ms before shipping. Any quota, error or latency failure falls back to the static lexical path. No card, no bill.

BUILD EFFORT
About 22-28 engineer-days for one full-stack developer with LLM assistance: data pipeline and normalization 4-5 days; client application, search, cards, RTL/LTR, i18n, accessibility and no-JS pages 6-8 days; concept lexicon 5-7 days and the long pole; 600-item evaluation and calibration 3-4 days; licensing and disclosure pages 1-2 days; two-host deployment and smoke tests 1-2 days. Ongoing: 2-4 hours per month for lexicon curation and an optional 1-2 hours per quarter for calibration. No dependencies to patch, no servers to upgrade, no certificates to renew and no API keys to rotate.

dataPipeline: Pin and commit the source. Copy Resources/quran-simple.txt byte-for-byte into the repository and track it. Record SHA-256 b3638f5cf03e2b05e4000efc0e4b656aafb3cf6ed28f8770b6497c5b43c46089, 1,353,702 bytes, 6,266 lines, 6,236 verses, 114 surahs and the 28-line Tanzil copyright block. Never regenerate or edit it. Write source URL, version, license and retrieval date to sources.lock.json.

Fetch translations at build time with no key. Make 114 calls to https://quranenc.com/api/v1/translation/sura/english_saheeh/{1..114} for v1.1.2 and the same for persian_ih v1.1.3. Fetch the published Talal Itani ClearQuran text. Freeze JSON under data/ with edition id, translator, publisher, version, license text, source URL and retrieval date. No runtime data API calls.

Fetch Tanzil quran-simple-clean.txt and quran-data.xml. Assert 6,236 verse lines in Simple Clean. Use Simple Clean only as an independent build-time cross-check, not as the index source. Use quran-data.xml for surah, juz, hizb, rub, page, sajda and English/Arabic names.

Validate alignment. Assert exactly 6,236 unique (surah, ayah) keys, 114 surahs and contiguous ayah numbering. Assert exactly one translation row per Arabic row for every shipped edition. Spot-check at least 20 verses including 1:1, 2:255, 18:10 and 112:1. Assert the display file hash and the presence of the copyright block.

Cross-check normalization. Normalize the display text and Simple Clean with the same Arabic normalizer. Assert at least 99.5% normalized agreement and log every mismatch with surah:ayah and both strings. Fail the build only on structural errors, not on legitimate Imlaei versus Simple Clean orthography differences.

Build display artifacts. Emit data/verses/001.json through 114.json with Arabic verbatim, shipped translations, and one verse before and after. Display files contain no normalized text. A byte-equality test asserts display Arabic equals the pinned source for every verse.

Build index-only normalized copies on a separate code path. Arabic: NFC; delete U+064B-U+065F, U+0670, U+0640 and U+06D6-U+06ED; fold alef variants to alef, ta marbuta to heh, alef maqsura to yeh, hamza carriers to their base; collapse whitespace. Persian: NFC; ZWNJ to separator; Arabic yeh and kaf to Persian; Persian and Arabic-Indic digits to ASCII; strip marks; preserve peh, cheh, jeh, gaf and Persian yeh. English: NFC, lowercase, punctuation strip, light plural fold. Store the analyzer version in every artifact header.

Build the concept lexicon. 300 concepts at launch and 500 as the target, each with 6-12 English synonyms, 6-12 Persian synonyms and 3-8 Arabic roots or lemmas. Bilingual Persian and Arabic religious review. Version the JSON and document it as the single ongoing human-curation surface.

Build BM25 indexes. Per-language field indexes for Arabic, English and Persian with k1=1.2 and b=0.75. Serialize QIDX1: magic, vocabulary count, document count, front-coded sorted term dictionary, varint delta postings of doc id and term frequency, then a Uint16 document-length array. Use dense verse ids 0-6235 mapped to (surah, ayah). Content-hash filenames, compress with gzip and Brotli, and build a 1,200-verse lite index for Save-Data and 2G.

Train and export the gates. Domain classifier: hashed character 3-5 gram plus unigram logistic regression over five classes, trained on 3,000-5,000 synthetic or edited English and Persian queries plus 500 hand-labeled gold items, exported as int8 weights about 300 KB. Sufficiency model: logistic regression over top-1 score, top-1/top-5 margin, BM25 z-score, content-term coverage, cross-field consensus, query length, domain probability and exact-reference flag. Train on 600 labeled items, 300 English and 300 Persian, half answerable, with 25% unanswerable or off-topic, 15% fiqh-boundary and 10% sensitive. Export about 1 KB of weights. Native Persian review is mandatory. No training at runtime.

Calibrate thresholds on held-out folds. Choose per-language thresholds for at most 2% false answers on unanswerable items and at most 10% false refusals on answerable items, with a stretch target of 5%. Record thresholds, analyzer versions, index hashes, edition versions and calibration dates in data/meta.json. Never hardcode a threshold or copy 0.38, 0.42 or 0.45 from another deployment.

Build the UI and static pages. Routes /en and /fa, a Web Worker search module, the Verse Card renderer, RTL and LTR layouts, i18n catalogs, 114 pre-rendered surah pages per language, 300 concept topic pages, a licenses page reproducing the seven QuranEnc conditions and the Tanzil attribution, a privacy page and accessible error states. The build fails if any i18n key is missing in either locale.

Freeze and verify. Commit every artifact rather than rebuilding in CI. Write a SHA-256 for each artifact to meta.json. The client verifies hashes before parsing. A golden test of 100 queries, including 2:255 to Al-Baqarah 255, patience to 2:153 in English and Persian, and الرحمن despite the corpus storing tatweel plus superscript alef, blocks deployment. The test asserts display Arabic byte equality and 6,236 aligned rows.

Deploy and mirror. Publish to Cloudflare Pages as primary and GitHub Pages as a byte-identical mirror. Configure DNS failover, immutable caching for hashed assets, CSP default-src self and no analytics or cookies. Run a 50-query smoke test per language after deployment.
final.retrievalSpec:
All retrieval runs in a module Web Worker. There are no network calls at query time; the only network is the initial static asset fetch. The app loads meta.json first, verifies its version and hash, then loads the active language pack. An English pack contains the English index plus the shared Arabic expansion index; a Persian pack contains the Persian index plus the shared Arabic index. The other language pack is fetched only on a deliberate language switch. The total per pack is roughly 1.8-2.8 MB gzip. Assets use content-hashed filenames and Cache-Control public, max-age=31536000, immutable. If hash verification fails, the app shows the pre-rendered surah pages and never a partial answer.

Query flow:
1. Input sanitation. Trim, HTML-escape at render, strip bidi controls U+202A-U+202E and U+2066-U+2069, cap at 500 characters, reject empty or under 2 characters with the short-input copy, and detect script. Queries are never inserted into HTML.
2. Reference resolution. Parse 2:255, 2.255, 2/255, Al-Baqarah 255, Surah 2 Ayah 255, سوره بقره آیه ۲۵۵, آیه ۲۵۵ بقره and Arabic-script equivalents, with a 114-name alias table in English, Persian and Arabic and digit normalization. A valid reference returns that verse plus one verse before and after, bypassing retrieval gates. A syntactically reference-like but out-of-range input returns a clarification with the valid range; it never guesses a nearby verse.
3. Domain classification. A hashed character 3-5 gram plus unigram logistic classifier returns five probabilities. P(off_topic) at or above 0.80 returns refused_off_topic with no retrieval. P(fiqh) at or above 0.55 routes to boundary mode. P(personal_guidance) at or above 0.55 routes to reflection cards. P(history) at or above 0.55 permits Quranic verses only. If no class reaches 0.60, the query retrieves and the sufficiency model decides. These values are bootstrap settings and are refit on the calibration set.
4. Normalization. Apply the exact build-time functions for the detected language. Persian is two-stage: ZWNJ to separator, Persian and Arabic-Indic digits to ASCII, Arabic yeh and kaf to Persian, then the shared Arabic fold. Arabic is NFC, strip U+064B-U+065F, U+0670, U+0640 and U+06D6-U+06ED, fold alef variants, ta marbuta, alef maqsura and hamza carriers. English is NFC, lowercase, punctuation strip and light plural fold. Persian letters peh, cheh, jeh, gaf and Persian yeh survive every step.
5. Concept expansion. Each content term is looked up in concepts.json, producing English, Persian and Arabic root or lemma term sets. Unmapped terms pass through unchanged. Expansion is capped at eight terms per content word to prevent drift. This lexicon is the only cross-lingual bridge in v1; there is no runtime translation and no LLM.
6. BM25 retrieval. Run BM25 with k1=1.2 and b=0.75 over the loaded field indexes. Query-language field weight is 1.0. Arabic expansion weight is 0.85. The other-language expansion weight is 0.6 only if that pack is explicitly loaded. Keep the top 50 per index.
7. Score aggregation. Per verse, take max(field score) plus 0.15 times min(2, number of fields with a hit). An exact phrase hit in the normalized verse text adds 0.2. A valid verse-reference match overrides all scoring and returns the referenced verse directly.
8. Fusion and diversity. Fuse the ranked lists with reciprocal rank fusion, k=60. Take the top 40. Apply MMR over normalized content-token sets using Jaccard similarity, lambda=0.7, with a maximum of two verses per surah. Return the top five cards, range three to eight.
9. Sufficiency. The learned model scores top-1, top-1/top-5 margin, BM25 z-score, content-term coverage, cross-field consensus, query length, domain probability and exact-reference flag. If P(answerable) is below the calibrated per-language threshold, return refused_no_retrieval. The deterministic fallback requires content-term coverage at least 0.34 and top-1 at least theta_lang; theta_en 3.2 and theta_fa 3.0 are bootstrap values only, not validated constants.
10. Render. Show Arabic first, then the user-language translation, a collapsed second edition, one verse before and after, quran.com and tanzil.net links, the exact disclosure and a terms-I-searched-for panel. The panel lists matched terms and the gate that fired. It is local-only and never transmitted.

Parameters and calibration:
- BM25 k1=1.2, b=0.75; field weights 1.0 active language and 0.85 Arabic; 0.6 for an explicitly loaded third language.
- RRF k=60; MMR lambda=0.7; maximum two verses per surah; five cards, range three to eight.
- Sufficiency features as above; thresholds per language, fitted on the 600-item eval. Calibration targets: at most 2% false answers on unanswerable items, at most 10% false refusals on answerable items, stretch 5%, and refusal precision at least 95%.
- No fixed cosine thresholds. The 0.38, 0.42 and 0.45 values are prohibited because no primary source calibrates them for bge-m3 on Arabic or Persian. The Phase 2 dense path uses its own calibrated threshold.

Latency and fallbacks:
- Index load is one-time, 0.9-1.4 MB gzip per language plus the shared Arabic index; parsing is expected in 30-80 ms on a mid-range Android. Query latency after load is 15-40 ms. A lite 1,200-verse index is served on Save-Data or 2G. The full index is immutable-cached.
- If the index fails to load or verify, show the 114 pre-rendered surah pages per language and the 300 concept pages. The Q&A box is progressive enhancement only.
- If the gate model fails to load, fall back to the deterministic coverage and theta gates. If those are unavailable, refuse with the no-retrieval copy. Never answer from model memory.
- There is no embedding model in v1. The Phase 2 dense path is optional, uses a Worker plus D1 plus Workers AI bge-m3, and hard-fails to this static lexical path on any quota, error or latency breach.

Quality measurement:
- Recall@10, MRR@10 and nDCG@10 per language; refusal precision and false-refusal rate per language; citation validity at 100%; cold-load completion and model/index hash failures. Because there is no telemetry, these are measured by the committed, locally run eval harness and by user-initiated reports copied to the clipboard, not by server logs.
- The 600-item eval is 300 English and 300 Persian, half answerable, with 25% unanswerable or off-topic, 15% fiqh-boundary and 10% sensitive. QRCD v1.2, AyaTEC v1.2 and IslamicFaithQA are auxiliary only; QRCD and AyaTEC are Arabic, and the Hugging Face dataset named tarteel-ai/quranqa is QRCD, not AyaTEC. No Persian Quran QA benchmark was found; that absence is bounded by the searches performed, so the internal Persian set is mandatory.
final.refusalSpec:
Statuses: answered, answered_with_boundary, refused_off_topic, refused_no_retrieval. Every response carries mode card and generated_commentary false in v1. Refusal is architectural first: the renderer cannot emit a verse that did not come from the pinned corpus. It is gate-based second.

G0 Input sanity. Empty input, under 2 characters, over 500 characters, non-text or a control-token pattern returns a clarification with no retrieval. Copy: English Please ask a shorter question about the Quran. Persian لطفاً پرسشی کوتاه‌تر درباره قرآن بپرسید.

G1 Reference parsing. A valid verse reference resolves exactly and bypasses retrieval gates, but still receives the fiqh or sensitive notice if applicable. A reference-like but out-of-range input returns a clarification with the valid range. It never returns a nearest guessed verse and never invents a citation.

G2 Domain classification. P(off_topic) at or above 0.80 returns refused_off_topic with no retrieval. P(fiqh) at or above 0.55 routes to answered_with_boundary. P(personal_guidance) at or above 0.55 routes to reflection cards. P(history) at or above 0.55 allows Quranic verses only. If no class reaches 0.60, retrieve and let sufficiency decide. These thresholds are bootstrap values, refit on the eval; they are not copied constants.

G3 Sufficiency. The learned model over top-1, margin, z-score, coverage, consensus, query length, domain probability and exact-reference flag returns P(answerable). Below the calibrated per-language threshold, return refused_no_retrieval without any generated text. Deterministic fallback: coverage at least 0.34 and top-1 at least theta_lang; theta_en 3.2 and theta_fa 3.0 are placeholders only. The calibration target is at most 2% false answers and at most 10% false refusals, stretch 5%.

G4 Coverage. The learned model includes coverage; the deterministic fallback keeps the 0.34 floor only as a bootstrap. Coverage is matched content terms divided by total content terms. Lowering the honesty gate is not an acceptable fix for over-refusal; add lexicon synonyms instead.

G5 Fiqh. Markers include halal, haram, permissible, forbidden, obligatory, recommended, disliked, sin, ruling, fatwa, divorce, inheritance, حلال, حرام, واجب, مستحب, مکروه, مجاز, گناه, حکم شرعی, فتوا, طلاق, ارث. Such queries return answered_with_boundary: relevant verses only, never an inferred ruling. If no verse is retrieved, return refused_no_retrieval.

G6 Sensitive topics. War and violence, women and family, slavery, apostasy, punishment, marriage and divorce, inheritance, jihad, killing, LGBTQ, antisemitism and interfaith topics are held in internal config, never surfaced as a UI taxonomy. Render the complete verse, one verse before and after, at least two translations where available, and a neutral context panel with surah, revelation place and period. No editorial framing, no apology, no AI commentary and no violent or controversial label.

G7 Output contract. Validate the schema, verse ids, citation URLs, language and disclosure. v1 has no model-generated text, so there is no claim-level validator in the answer path; the validator is reserved for the optional Phase 3 prose tier. If a future prose draft fails any check, discard it and show cards.

Exact copy, do not paraphrase.
Off-topic English: I can only answer questions about the Quran. This question is outside that scope, so I cannot answer it.
Off-topic Persian: من فقط به پرسش‌هایی درباره قرآن پاسخ می‌دهم. این پرسش خارج از این حوزه است و نمی‌توانم به آن پاسخ دهم.
No-retrieval English: I could not find a Quranic verse relevant to this question, so I cannot answer it. Try rephrasing with Quranic terms, or consult a qualified scholar.
No-retrieval Persian: هیچ آیه‌ای از قرآن مرتبط با این پرسش پیدا نکردم؛ بنابراین نمی‌توانم به آن پاسخ دهم. لطفاً پرسش را با واژه‌های قرآنی بازنویسی کنید یا با عالمی واجد شرایط مشورت کنید.
Fiqh boundary English: The Quran addresses this topic, but a ruling (fatwa) requires a qualified mufti. The relevant verses are shown below; this is not a fatwa.
Fiqh boundary Persian: قرآن درباره این موضوع آیاتی دارد، اما صدور حکم شرعی (فتوا) فقط از سوی مفتی واجد شرایط ممکن است. آیات مرتبط در ادامه آمده است؛ این پاسخ فتوا نیست.
Sensitive context English: Read in context: the full verse and adjacent verses are shown. Translations and interpretations differ; only the Arabic Quranic text is authoritative.
Sensitive context Persian: در بافت بخوانید: آیه کامل و آیات مجاور نمایش داده شده است. ترجمه‌ها و تفسیرها متفاوت‌اند؛ تنها متن عربی قرآن مرجع است.
Language scope English: This service currently answers only in English and Persian.
Language scope Persian: این خدمت در حال حاضر فقط به انگلیسی و فارسی پاسخ می‌دهد.
Standing disclaimer English: This site shows Quranic verses and translations. It does not provide tafsir, fatwas, or religious rulings. For a ruling, consult a qualified scholar.
Standing disclaimer Persian: این سایت آیات و ترجمه‌های قرآن را نمایش می‌دهد و تفسیر، فتوا یا حکم شرعی ارائه نمی‌کند. برای دریافت حکم شرعی با عالم واجد شرایط مشورت کنید.
Translation label English: Translation is interpretation, not the Quran.
Translation label Persian: ترجمه، تفسیر است، نه خود قرآن.

Calibration and governance. 600 labeled items, 300 English and 300 Persian, half answerable, with 25% unanswerable or off-topic, 15% fiqh-boundary and 10% sensitive, reviewed natively in both languages. Targets: false answers at most 2%, false refusals at most 10% with a 5% stretch, refusal precision at least 95%, citation validity 100%. Re-fit quarterly or when the lexicon or index changes. A scholar board reviews 100 random answers per month and every sensitive card before launch. QRCD v1.2 and AyaTEC v1.2 provide auxiliary Arabic no-answer and zero-answer items; IslamicFaithQA provides Arabic and English abstention items. The Hugging Face dataset tarteel-ai/quranqa is QRCD, not AyaTEC. No Persian Quran QA benchmark was found, so the internal Persian set is mandatory; the absence claim is bounded by the searches performed.

Fallback behavior. If the index fails, show the 114 pre-rendered surah pages per language and the 300 concept pages. If the domain model fails, use conservative rules and then sufficiency. If the sufficiency model fails, use the deterministic coverage and theta gates. If those fail, return refused_no_retrieval. There is no LLM, no model memory and no server. Nothing can bill, and no question leaves the device.
